title: An AI Fraud Kingpin’s Confessions
content:
For months I’ve been speaking to an AI fraud kingpin. You might remember in 2024 we revealed the existence of OnlyFake, an underground site that let anyone generate realistic photos of fake IDs using ‘neural networks’. The creator of that site went by the handle John Wick. A while later, the creator was arrested.

Turns out there was a lot more to that story. Yuriy Nazarenko, the creator of OnlyFake, told me his side of it. How when I published my initial article he panicked, and destroyed his laptop and emails and got a new phone, paranoid that authorities were about to bust down his door. How the pressure of a growing fraud empire pushed him to drugs. And how North Korean fake IT workers used his site. Read below for his story. 

A few years ago, Yuriy Nazarenko sat at a desk in his grandfather’s apartment in Ukraine and, on a diet of cigarettes, Lay’s chips, and beer, painstakingly made digital copies of fake identity documents. One of his four computer screens had the messaging app Telegram open. Another displayed a scan of a passport in Photoshop filling the entire monitor.

title: CSC:lle ikäsertifikaatti tunnustuksena monimuotoisesta ja yhdenvertaisesta työyhteisöstä
content:
Excellence Finlandin myöntämän ikäsertifikaatin saavat vastuullisesti toimivat organisaatiot, jotka edistävät ikätasa-arvoa työelämässä. Tunnustus on tärkeä osoitus siitä, että kaikenikäisiä työntekijöitä kohdellaan tasapuolisesti niin rekrytoinnissa kuin urakehityksessä.

CSC:llä monimuotoisuus ja yhdenvertaisuus ovat niin strateginen kuin päivittäisessä työssä näkyvä teema.

Rekrytoinneissa pyritään tavoittamaan monipuolinen hakijajoukko eri ikäryhmistä. Valinnat tehdään osaamisen, kokemuksen ja tehtävään soveltuvuuden perusteella. Myös nuorten työelämään siirtymistä tuetaan eri alojen harjoittelupaikkojen tarjoamisella. title: Exploring the Nature, History, and Culture of Kalimantan with WikiBanua
content: WikiBanua is a documentation project focused on cultural heritage sites, landmarks, natural landscapes, and public facilities across Kalimantan. Following its successful implementation in various locations throughout South Kalimantan—supported by a grant from Wikimedia Indonesia through the “Dana Wiki” program—WikiBanua expanded its reach into neighboring provinces, Central Kalimantan and East Kalimantan, under the initiatives “WikiBanua 3.0” and “WikiBanua 4.0.” Unlike previous iterations, this phase of WikiBanua was managed by a two-person team: Ilham Mufti Laksono (User:Ilham Mufti Laksono) as Project Manager and Arief Rahman (User:Ezagren) as Assistant Project Manager, both of whom are members of the Wikimedia Banjar Community. Nevertheless, the project proved successful thanks to the involvement of local volunteers and contributors to Wikimedia projects across South, Central, and East Kalimantan, who participated in a range of WikiBanua activities, including documentation efforts, workshops, and in-person meetups.

title: HP nimittää Emma Walmsleyn toimitusjohtajaksi
content:
PALO ALTO, Kalifornia, 4.11.2026 – HP Inc:n (NYSE: HPQ) hallitus on yksimielisesti nimittänyt Emma Walmsleyn yhtiön toimitusjohtajaksi 4.1.2027 alkaen. Walmsley toimi viimeksi GSK:n toimitusjohtajana, ja hän on ollut Microsoftin hallituksen jäsen seitsemän vuotta. Hän seuraa tehtävässä Bruce Broussardia, joka on toiminut väliaikaisena toimitusjohtajana helmikuusta 2026. Broussard siirtyy samana päivänä hallituksen puheenjohtajaksi Chip Berghin tilalle.

”HP:llä on valtavasti potentiaalia nyt, kun teknologia on tärkeässä murroskohdassa. Tarvitsemme johtajan, joka rakentaa innovaatioperinteemme ja vahvuuksiemme varaan ja muovaa rohkeasti yhtiön tulevaisuutta. Emma on toimitusjohtajana näyttänyt, että hän osaa johtaa suuria organisaatioita ja viedä niitä isojen muutosten läpi. Hänellä on kokemusta ja taitoa koota HP:n liiketoiminnat, osaaminen ja ihmiset yhteen, jotta voimme tarttua mahdollisuuksiin, joita tekoälyn siirtyminen laitteisiin tarjoaa. Tekoäly muuttaa samalla työntekoa ja arkea yhä verkottuneemmassa maailmassa. Tuen häntä mielelläni, kun hän vie HP:n seuraavaan kasvuvaiheeseen”, sanoo väliaikainen toimitusjohtaja Bruce Broussard.

content:
Cyrus Walther is a doctoral student in the Astroparticle Physics Group at TU Dortmund University; nominated by IUPAP, he has served on the CODATA Executive Committee since 2023. He contributes actively to CODATA’s Early Career Group, CODATA Connect, and to the Task Group on Digital Representation of Units of Measure (DRUM).

From the 19th to the 21st of October, the International Science Council (ISC), in collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Technology (CAST), welcomed the international scientific community to Beijing for the Beijing Science Dialogue. During these three days, topics of transformative impact on science were discussed, among them Artificial Intelligence. As AI especially impacts early- and mid-career researchers, EMCRs from the ISC community suggested including young panellists on the topic. Following a nomination, I had the great honour to receive that invitation from the International Science Council to speak as an early-career scientist on the panel “Responsible AI for global challenges”.

title: Uusi julkaisu: Digitaalinen teknologia muokkaa perhesuhteita
content:
Family Relationships in the Digital Era -kirja kokoaa yhteen johtavia tutkijoita tarkastelemaan, miten digitaaliset teknologiat ovat kietoutuneet perhe-elämään, ja voivat sekä yhdistää että etäännyttää perhesuhteita.

Kirja ei ota kantaa siihen, onko teknologia perhe-elämälle hyväksi vai haitaksi, vaan kokoaa yhteen viimeisen reilun vuosikymmenen tutkimustulokset ja tarjoaa näin monipuolisen, tutkimukseen perustuvan tilannekuvan aiheesta. Teos luo katsauksen satoihin tutkimuksiin ja niihin perustuen läpileikkaaviksi teemoiksi muodostuu kaksi tärkeää näkökulmaa. Ensinnäkin digitaalinen teknologia on muuttanut perheiden ajankäyttöä ja huomion kohdentumista, mutta samalla laajentanut merkittävästi mahdollisuuksia pitää yhteyttä perheenjäseniin. Toisena merkittävänä teemana teoksen läpi kulkee ymmärrys siitä, että ihmismieli kantaa yhä mukanaan perhe-elämän evolutiivista perintöä nopeasta teknologisesta muutoksesta huolimatta.

title: Finskspråkigt språkcafé: Julpyssel och julstämning
content:
Tid: Lördag 5 december 2026 kl. 12.00–14.00
Plats: Finlandsinstitutet i Stockholm, Snickarbacken 4
Anmälan: Kostnadsfritt och ingen föranmälan krävs. Språkcaféet fungerar enligt drop in-principen. Barn under 10 år behöver delta tillsammans med en vårdnadshavare.

Välkommen till Finlandsinstitutets tredje och sista finskspråkiga språkcafé för hösten!

På självständighetsdagens afton samlas vi för att njuta av en avslappnad och stämningsfull eftermiddag med julpyssel. Kom och skapa juldekorationer och julkort, öva finska på ett kreativt sätt och upplev väntan på julen tillsammans med andra deltagare.

Utöver pysslandet bjuder vi på kaffe, te och dadelkaka. Språkcaféet passar alla åldrar, från barn till vuxna, som talar eller förstår finska eller är intresserade av finsk och sverigefinsk kultur.

På språkcaféet används finskan på ett avslappnat och kravlöst sätt. Genom kreativa aktiviteter, samtal och gemensamt skapande får deltagarna möjlighet att träna finska, utöka sitt ordförråd och träffa andra som är intresserade av det finska språket.

title: Korjaus aiemmin tänään lähetettyyn tiedotteeseen: Hämeenlinnan taidemuseon teosäänestyksen ensimmäiset voittajat selvillä – yleisön suosikit pääsevät esille Lohrmann-rakennukseen
content:
Juhlavuoden teosäänestyksen takana on ajatus tarjota yleisölle mahdollisuus tutustua taidemuseon erilaisiin kokoelmiin ja vaikuttaa siihen, mitkä teokset nousevat esille. Äänestys järjestetään kahdessa osassa, ja mukana on keräilijöiden tallettamia kokoelmia (Niemistö-kokoelma ja Vexi Salmen kokoelma) ja taiteilijoiden lahjoittamia kokoelmia (Ester Heleniuksen ja Maija Isolan kokoelmat) sekä taidemuseon oma kokoelma.

Niemistö-kokoelman ehdokasteoksista voittajaksi valikoitui Jarmo Mäkilän (s.1952) öljymaalaus Karanteeni. Teos on talletettu Hämeenlinnan taidemuseoon vuonna 2020, ja on ollut aiemmin esillä Meidän valintamme -näyttelyssä 2022. Karanteeni on nähtävillä 4.12.2026–10.1.2027.

Niemistö-kokoelmasta äänestettiin esille lisäksi kolmen videoteoksen joukosta Pekka Luukkolan blue ray- videoluuppi Sense of Time (kesto 02:01). Teos on nähty aiemmin muun muassa Goodmanin kauppakeskuksessa 2022 ja Hämeenlinnan taidemuseossa Henki ja Hekuma – Väristyksiä kokoelmista -näyttelyssä 2025. Sense of Time talletettiin Niemistö-kokoelmaan 2012. Videoteoksen voi kokea 4.12.2026 alkaen Lohrmann-rakennuksen alakerrassa.

title: Nya nätverk tar itu med strukturella utmaningar inom kultursektorn
content:
– Många sökande tog upp strukturella frågor inom sina respektive områden: tillgång till yrkesmässiga möjligheter, rättvisa arbetsvillkor, representation, konstnärlig självständighet, kunskapsutbyte och kulturorganisationernas hållbarhet. Detta gav ansökningsomgången en stark yrkesmässig och social dimension, säger Denisas Kolomyckis, ordförande för expertgruppen.

– En annan tendens är att inkludering behandlas som en metod, och vi ser att uppmärksamhet riktas mot geografiska periferiområden – flera nätverk betraktade periferin som en produktiv utgångspunkt snarare än en brist, fortsätter han.

Som vanligt var många av nätverksansökningarna kopplade till festivaler, konferenser, showcase-evenemang och andra befintliga evenemang. Denisas Kolomyckis konstaterar att sådana evenemang kan vara värdefulla mötesplatser och ofta utgör ett effektivt sätt att föra samman yrkesverksamma.

Itsenäisyyspäivän aattona kokoonnumme viettämään rentoa ja tunnelmallista iltapäivää jouluaskartelun merkeissä. Tule valmistamaan jouluisia koristeita ja kortteja, harjoittelemaan suomea luovalla tavalla sekä nauttimaan joulun odotuksesta yhdessä muiden osallistujien kanssa.

title: Culture gains a stronger name and place in the European Parliament’s Horizon Europe compromise
content:
Culture Action Europe is proud to be part of the Name Place Fund coalition, which brings together culture and research organisations advocating for stronger support for culture in Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund. We welcome the cross-party compromise text on Horizon Europe 2028-2034 negotiated in the European Parliament. 

It was prepared by rapporteurs Christian Ehler (EPP) and René Repasi (S&D) together with the shadow rapporteurs. The compromise is scheduled for a vote in Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Committee on 10 November. This text will be the starting point for the Parliament’s negotiations with the Commission and the Council. 

After long negotiations, culture, creativity and artistic research finally have a more prominent place in the future EU research and innovation programme.

Working with Prof. Brimblecombe

How can climate projections help heritage professionals decide which monument needs attention first? And what does adaptation mean for a mountain community whose landscape and traditions are threatened by recurring wildfires? These were among the questions that heritage professionals and researchers brought to Athens for the first Seasonal School of the European Partnership for Resilient Cultural Heritage (RCH).

The Heritage Management Organization (HERITΛGE) delivered the school, Heritage Adaptation to Climate Change, from 5 to 15 October 2026. More than 400 applications were filed from around the world. Fourteen participants attended in person at the European Parliament’s Europa Experience in Athens, and more than 100 took part online. The in-person participants were selected from candidates nominated by states participating in RCH. They represented 13 countries, with two participants from Spain and one each from Belgium, Croatia, Egypt, Finland, Greece, Italy, Lithuania, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Romania and the United Kingdom.

title: If Fritz Lang’s Iconic Film Metropolis Had a Kraftwerk Soundtrack
content:
The case of the copyright history of Fritz Lang’s influential sci-fi masterpiece Metropolis is as convoluted as the history of its film print. Lang’s vision and his original almost-three-hour cut were doomed to censorship right from the start. The Nazis took out its more socialist scenes. It’s been edited, colorized, put back together and restored. Wikipedia currently lists nine different versions. Similarly, ownership of the film shifted from distributors back to the public domain, then out of it again, once more of the original footage was rediscovered. And then came 2023, when Metropolis once again landed in the public domain, at least in America. Will we see as many legal battles as new remixes and re-scores? Probably a bit of both.

The film’s original orchestral score is available, but many fans also seek out a score more befitting its futurist origins. Something more electronic.

title: Europe: Get Satellites or Get Throttled
content:
European powers must urgently break Elon Musk’s near-monopoly over military communications. It won’t be easy. It won’t be cheap. It won’t happen fast. But it’s necessary to ensure no one man can repeat the trillionaire’s treatment of Ukraine in early October, when he throttled Ukraine’s access to the Starlink and Starshield satellite systems now central to its military operations.

Starlink is a commercial satellite communications service, with Starshield a more capable military version. Both belong to Musk’s SpaceX. Ukraine — and many other Western powers, for that matter — relies on them for an array of vital military functions. They connect troops to their headquarters and drones to their operators.

Overnight and without warning in mid-October, thousands of satellite terminals failed in Ukraine. Operators discovered that SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of approximately 160 kmh (100 mph) or slower. Above that speed, a drone couldn’t connect to its operator. Many of the faster drones, including interceptor drones that Ukraine uses to defeat Russia’s own attack drones, couldn’t function.

title: US midterms delivered a blow to tech’s AI ambitions
content:
There’s no question the US midterms elections delivered a blow to Donald Trump. The Democrats took not just the House and Senate back from the Republicans, but won a wave of governor’s races across the country — including in states it would’ve previously been hard to imagine a Democrat winning.

But it wasn’t just Trump who lost. The tech industry and its ambitions to cover the country in hyperscale data centers to power generative AI were potentially even bigger losers than the orange man himself.

It didn’t matter that Elon Musk shelled out over $400 million to try to save Republicans as polling increasingly suggested a wipeout was coming, especially in his chosen home of Texas, or that crypto and AI companies deployed millions more on races across the country. An NBC News exit poll still found 56% of voters said AI and data centers were “crucial or a major factor” in their vote for Congress. And it showed in the results.

title: Metsola tells MEPs not to rely on AI when drafting laws
content:
European Parliament President Roberta Metsola warned MEPs Wednesday not to be overreliant on AI in decision-making, as the Parliament prepares new guidelines for lawmakers on how to use it.

“Drafting an amendment with the help of AI cannot replace fundamentally the constructive debate with a colleague,” she said at an event on AI use in the Parliament. “Doing legal research with the help of AI cannot ultimately replace the judgment and the critical thinking needed to make a tough decision.”

Metsola said there must be “democratic accountability” in lawmaking and argued that “where AI is used, people should know.”

“No matter how AI may be used in a parliament, the responsibility is still [with] those who are elected,” she said.

Secretary-General Alessandro Chiocchetti said at the same event that Parliament is building its own AI tool for sensitive work, hosted on its internal infrastructure.

As POLITICO reported in July, commercial AI models, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Meta’s Llama, can still be used for less sensitive tasks.

title: Belgium: ‘Divisive’ migration home raids law must be voted down by parliament
content:
Ahead of the vote in Belgian Federal Parliament on Thursday 5 November on whether to allow police raids on people’s homes for migration control purposes, including homes of people who may be hosting undocumented migrants, Dinushika Dissanayake the Deputy Regional Director of Amnesty International said:

“These proposals which allow for home raids are bound to sow fear and division. The bill before Belgium’s parliament gives police vast powers to enter people’s homes for migration control purposes, between the hours of 5am and 9pm and irrespective of whether children are present.

“This would not only cause a serious intrusion into people’s private and family life but also the bill fails to provide effective ways to appeal or challenge these decisions.

“Belgium has a strong tradition of showing solidarity towards migrant communities, with many people opening their doors and homes to offer beds, food and support – as is their prerogative. This will discourage people from doing so in future.

“These disproportionate powers are another cruel and coercive tool to create an increasingly hostile environment for migrants in Europe and for those showing solidarity with them.

title: The 2027 Mark Palmer Prize: Call for Nominations
content:
Freedom House is now accepting nominations for the 2027 Mark Palmer Prize, inviting individuals and organizations around the world to put forward candidates whose work exemplifies the important role of diplomacy in supporting democratic movements and defending fundamental freedoms.

The award takes its name from the late Mark Palmer, a longtime Freedom House trustee and US ambassador to Hungary from 1986 to 1990. In 1989, as the Cold War was coming to a close, Palmer boldly joined civil society and the Hungarian democratic opposition to support the country’s transition to democracy.
 
The Mark Palmer Prize has been awarded to diplomats and international civil servants from around the world, including Georgia, Peru, the Czech Republic, Lithuania, Mongolia, Sweden, Canada, Uruguay, and the United States. The prize is made possible through the generosity of the Mark and Sushma Palmer Legacy Fund, established by Dr. Sushma Palmer in loving memory of her late husband and former Freedom House trustee and vice chairman Ambassador Mark Palmer.

title: The scandals and suspects surrounding Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the Brazilian press
content:
After being defeated in the elections, the senator fled to the US with his family

Originally published on Global Voices

Art by Global Voices with Canva Pro. Photo by the Brazilian Senate. Fair use.

Forty-eight hours after losing the runoff in Brazil to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Flávio Bolsonaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro’s eldest son, a senator representing Rio de Janeiro, fled to the United States. From there, where his brother Eduardo, a former congressman, has lived since February 2025, he continues to challenge the results of the election he lost by 4.4 million votes, as attested by the Electoral Court (TSE), the Organization of American States (OAS), and other right-led governments in the region.

Upon landing in Miami, Flávio published a letter proclaiming himself “the true president of Brazil” and “president-elect of Brazil.” After 22 minutes — and a demand from the US Department of State — he retracted to “the leader of Brazil.”

title: January Protests: Another Protester Sentenced to Death Identified in Mashhad
content:
According to HRANA, Vahid Khodrikhah, 34, a resident of Mashhad, has been identified as another of the three individuals sentenced to death in connection with the January 2026 protests in the city.

Vahid Khodrikhah, along with Matin Farnian, 23, and another individual, was sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, on the charge of “moharebeh” (enmity against God).

HRANA had previously reported the issuance of death sentences against these three individuals. However, at that time, only Matin Farnian’s identity had been confirmed. With the identification of Vahid Khodrikhah, the identities of two defendants in the case have now been established, while efforts to identify the third individual are ongoing.

An informed source told HRANA regarding Khodrikhah’s physical condition: “Before his arrest, he was wounded by gunfire during the January protests. The bullet has since been removed from his body, and the necessary follow-up medical care has been provided during his imprisonment.”

title: OPINION: Our Insignificance
content:
By Jonathan Power*

LUND, Sweden | 4 November 2026 (IDN) — “Suppose aliens existed, and that some had been watching our planet for its entire forty-five million centuries, what would they have seen? Over most of that vast time-span, Earth’s appearance altered very gradually. Continents drifted; ice-cover waxed and waned; successive species emerged, evolved and became extinct.

“But just in a tiny sliver of Earth’s history—the last hundred centuries—the patterns of vegetation altered much faster than before. This signalled the start of agriculture—and then urbanization.”

We are at the very end of that “sliver”.

So begins a book by Martin Rees, Britain’s former Astronomer Royal, On the Future: Prospects for Humanity.

There is much in this short, very readable book—the disturbing, sometimes positive, sometimes negative, future of biotech, artificial intelligence, global warming, medicine, ageing, communications, nuclear energy, weapons development, sustainability, agricultural research, poverty and employment—but its centrepiece is astronomy.

The association will coordinate the movement for open, decentralised and interoperable social media in Europe. European.Social began as a shared manifesto, launched on 5 June 2026 at the PublicSpaces Conference with 12 founding signatories – including PublicSpaces. title: Pekingin pitkä käsi – Toimitusketjujen läpinäkyvyyttä koetellaan jälleen, kun Kiina rakentaa ekstraterritoriaalista sääntelyään
content:
Kiina on pitkään arvostellut Yhdysvaltojen tapaa ulottaa pakotteensa, vientirajoituksensa ja sääntelynsä maan rajojen ulkopuolelle. Nyt Peking pyrkii rakentamaan omaa “pitkää kättään” ja sitä kautta vaikuttamaan yritysten ja yksilöiden toimintaan myös omien rajojensa ulkopuolella. Ennen kaikkea hallinnon tarkoituksena on vaikeuttaa tai estää ulkomaisten toimitusketjuja koskevien vaatimusten toimeenpanoa silloin, kun niiden katsotaan vahingoittavan Kiinan etuja. 

Kiinan valtioneuvoston keväällä 2026 antamat asetukset 834 ja 835 ovat uusi ase suurvaltojen välisessä kauppasodassa. Asetus 834 (“toimitusketjujen turvallisuusasetus”) antaa Kiinan viranomaisille valtuudet seurata, suojata ja tarvittaessa puuttua toimitusketjuihin liittyviin riskeihin. Asetus 835 (“ulkomaiden ekstraterritoriaalisen lainkäytön vastainen asetus”) puolestaan mahdollistaa sen, että Kiina voi tunnistaa tiettyjä ulkomaisia lakeja tai viranomaistoimia ”epäasianmukaisiksi” ja kieltää niiden noudattamisen.

title: Burning questions about burning trash
content: Depending on where you live, your waste can take several routes. About half of the waste in the EU gets recycled or composted, the rest ends up either in a landfill or a giant furnace. Burning waste in specialised plants can transform that waste into energy – something that Europe constantly needs more of. Sounds like a win-win? Not so fast. title: American Voters Overwhelmingly Reject AI Data Centers
content:
People across America rejected data centers during last night’s midterm election. Proposals related to data centers were explicitly on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states. People voted against data centers in 38 of them and counting. Six cities voted to ban data centers outright and 12 put limits on the amount of megawatts such buildings could draw. In addition to specific ballot measures, candidates who supported data centers lost across the country.

One of the most striking repudiations of pro data center politicians was in Texas, where Gregg Abbott lost a bid for a fourth term as governor. Abbott had made Texas a data center friendly place. The state has more than 300 working data centers and there are plans to double that number. “Texas is the epicenter of AI development,” Abbott said in 2025 at a press conference with Google CEO Sundar Pichai. “We must ensure that America remains at the forefront of the AI revolution, and Texas is the place where that can happen.” He went on to accept more than $9 million from data center-related donors.

title: Iraq Jails Ex-Oil Boss for Eight Years Over $119M Kickback Scheme
content:
A high-profile court ruling against a senior former oil official has delivered another warning to Iraq’s political establishment that high office no longer guarantees impunity, an influential lawmaker told OCCRP on Wednesday, as authorities widen an aggressive anti-corruption campaign across the country’s lucrative energy sector.

The verdict sends “a clear message that positions and responsibilities do not grant immunity from accountability,” said Qaisar al-Jorani, a member of parliament’s committee on oil, gas, and natural resources, calling the misappropriation of state wealth a “red line that must not be crossed.”

The ruling, handed down by Iraq’s Criminal Court for Combating Corruption, sentenced Hussein Talib Abboud, the former director general of the State Company for Oil Products Distribution, to eight years in prison and ordered him to repay 55 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $36.2 million).

title: Vermont Was Supposed to Get an Audit of Its Lake Champlain Cleanup. It Never Happened.
content:
This summer, Vermont’s Clean Water Board celebrated a milestone: Over the past decade, the state has invested nearly a billion dollars to clean up its polluted streams, rivers and lakes. The vast majority of that money has gone toward Lake Champlain.

“I think that’s something to be extremely proud of,” said Douglas Farnham, the board’s chair.

Vermont was supposed to get an independent evaluation of what it has gotten for all that money. But that study was never done.

A decade ago, Vermont lawmakers mandated that the board submit an audit from an outside environmental consultant to determine whether the projects the state had invested in to improve water quality were working. The audit also was meant to examine whether the state’s agriculture and natural resource agencies are doing enough to enforce water quality regulations on farms, which are the biggest source of phosphorus in Lake Champlain.

Seven Days and ProPublica have teamed up to investigate the cleanup of Lake Champlain. Have you been affected by this issue? We’d like to hear from you.

title: Tekijänoikeuskorvaukset nousivat maailmalla ennätykselliseen 15,5 miljardiin euroon
content:
Tekijänoikeuskorvaukset kasvoivat globaalisti 11,3 prosenttia edellisvuodesta. Kasvua vauhdittivat erityisesti korvaukset digitaalisilta alustoilta, jotka muodostavat jo yli 40 prosenttia kaikista korvauksista. Digitaalisten korvausten kasvava merkitys alleviivaa reilujen pelisääntöjen tarvetta tekoälylle ja muille digialustoille.

Viimeisen viiden vuoden aikana luovista sisällöistä maksetut tekijänoikeuskorvaukset ovat olleet tasaisessa kasvussa. Vuonna 2025 korvauksia kerättiin maailmanlaajuisesti ennätykselliset 15,5 miljardia euroa. Musiikki on selvästi suurin tekijänoikeuskorvausten lähde.

Luvut käyvät ilmi tekijänoikeusjärjestöjen kansainvälisen kattojärjestön CISACin Global Collections Report 2026 -raportista. Raportti tarkastelee musiikin, audiovisuaalisten sisältöjen, visuaalisten taiteiden, kirjallisuuden ja näyttämötaiteen korvauksia. Raportissa on mukana 228 tekijänoikeusjärjestöä kaikkiaan 111 maasta.

title: Ukraine’s evolving international partnerships examined in collection of essays
content:
A collection of essays by five international experts reflects on how Ukraine’s relationships with countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East have evolved since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

CMI has published five short essays by journalists, academics and specialists in international relations and diplomacy that consider how external perceptions of Ukraine have shifted over the past four years. The authors trace some of Ukraine’s regional engagement strategies, and present opportunities and challenges for cooperation in the future.

The collection is a byproduct of CMI’s work in supporting relationships and mutual understanding between Ukrainian actors and international counterparts. According to Edward Marques, Head of CMI’s Eurasia Programme, the contributions “reflect the diversity of perspectives that now shape international discussions about Ukraine and, more broadly, about the future of international order.”

title: Kroatialainen Klara Bošnjak Fabijanić viettää eläkepäiviä tipujen ja älypuhelimen kanssa ja muistelee hyvällä Titon aikoja
content:
Autioituneiden rakennusten ikkunoista kurkottaa vihreinä rehottavia puiden oksia. Tienviertä reunustavat talot, joiden katot ovat romahtamaisillaan. Osa taloista on jäänyt keskeneräisiksi, jotkut seisovat tyhjillään, toisissa asutaan yhä.

Pohjois-Kroatian maaseutu on paikoittain karua katseltavaa: muuttoliike kaupunkeihin ja ulkomaille käy kuumana samalla, kun kylät pysyvät vaivoin pystyssä iäkkäiden asukkaiden ja satunnaisten paluumuuttajien ansiosta. Yksi tällaisista on 77-vuotias Klara Bošnjak Fabijanić.

”Tiesin aina, että eläkkeelle jäätyäni muuttaisin takaisin omaan pieneen kylääni.”

Kitinä on kova, kun Bošnjak Fabijanić nostaa sisäpihan kaivosta ämpärillisen kukkienkasteluvettä Unkarin rajalla, Drava-joen eteläpuolella, sijaitsevassa Podravska Moslavinan kylässä.

Sisällä olisi nykyisin myös juoksevaa vettä, mutta Bošnjak Fabijanić käyttää piha-askareisiin mieluummin samaa kaivoa, josta hän on nostanut vedet vuosikymmenten ajan.

Podravska Moslavina on Bošnjak Fabijanićin kotikylä ja koti, jossa hän asuu, hänen lapsuudenkotinsa.

Nyt paikalla on myös hänen tyttärensä, Marija Fabijani.

”Tämä paikka tuo minulle rauhan”, hän sanoo katsellen raukeana ympärilleen.

title: Lula’s victory in the 2026 Brazilian elections was far from inevitable
content:
On 25 October 2026, Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a fourth term in an election that exposed both the resilience of Brazilian democracy and the depth of the far right’s social roots. Lula received 51.79% of valid votes in the runoff against far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro’s 48.21%.

Three weeks earlier, however, the outcome had looked very different: Flávio - son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, now jailed for a coup attempt after losing his bid for reelection in 2022 - led the first round with 47.03% of the valid votes, compared with Lula’s 45.16%. The reversal was not simply an electoral comeback. It revealed how a campaign that had failed to generate enthusiasm could be transformed through collective mobilization, both online and in the streets.

The first round result was a warning against complacency. Lula’s campaign leaned heavily on his historical achievements and the restoration of policies associated with his previous Workers’ Party (PT) governments. These accomplishments were real, but they did not necessarily offer a persuasive answer to a question increasingly heard among voters: what comes next?

title: EU-komissio: Ukrainan on kiihdytettävä uudistusten tahtia saadakseen jäsenyysneuvottelunsa maaliin tavoiteajassa
content:
EU-komission mukaan Ukrainan täytyy nopeuttaa uudistustahtiaan, jos se haluaa saada EU-jäsenyysneuvottelunsa valmiiksi tavoitteensa mukaisesti vuoden 2028 loppuun mennessä.

Komission kanta käy ilmi sen keskiviikkona julkistamasta vuotuisesta laajentumisraportista.

- On tärkeää, että Ukraina jatkaa uudistusten tahdin kiihdyttämistä, jotta maa kykenee saavuttamaan kunnianhimoisen tavoitteensa saada liittymisneuvottelut päätökseen vuoden 2028 loppuun mennessä, komissio kirjoittaa tiedotteessaan.

Ukrainan on komission mukaan syytä keskittyä oikeusvaltioperiaatetta, demokraattisten instituutioiden toimintaa, julkishallinnon uudistamista ja kansallisia vähemmistöjä koskeviin uudistuksiin.

Ukraina haki EU:n jäsenyyttä maaliskuussa 2022 pian sen jälkeen, kun Venäjä oli aloittanut hyökkäyssotansa Ukrainaa vastaan.

KOMISSION mukaan jäsenyysneuvotteluissa on neljä edelläkävijämaata, joita Ukrainan lisäksi ovat Albania, Moldova ja Montenegro.

Montenegro on näistä maista jäsenyysprosessissaan kaikista pisimmällä, ja laajentumisraportin mukaan Montenegron jäsenyysneuvottelut voidaan saada valmiiksi vielä tänä vuonna.

title: Holopainen: Jääkiekko on Venäjälle osa valtion propagandaa
content:
Vihreiden kansanedustaja Mari Holopainen pitää Venäjän mahdollista pääsyä takaisin jääkiekon MM-kisoihin erittäin vaarallisena kehityksenä. Urheilun vetoomustuomioistuin CAS näytti Venäjän osallistumiselle vihreää valoa viime perjantaina.

CAS:in päätös ei koske vain Saksan jääkiekon MM-kisoja ensi toukokuussa vaan kaikkia Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliiton MM-turnauksia vuodesta 2027 alkaen. Ensimmäisenä vuorossa on jo vuodenvaihteessa Kanadassa pelattava alle 20-vuotiaiden MM-turnaus.

"Venäjä käy yhä hyökkäyssotaa Ukrainassa. Jääkiekko on Venäjälle paljon enemmän kuin urheilulaji, se on osa valtion propagandaa. On väärin normalisoida hyökkäyssotaa käyvän maan osallistuminen kisoihin", Holopainen sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Tänään uutisoitiin, että MM-kisojen pitkäaikainen pääsponsori Skoda Auto harkitsee nyt vetäytymistä turnauksen sponsoroinnista. Tähän mennessä useat jääkiekkomaajoukkueet ovat ilmoittaneet vastustavansa Venäjän paluuta. Suomen lisäksi Ruotsi, Tshekki, Norja, Tanska ja Latvia eivät aio pelata Venäjää vastaan.

Holopaisen mukaan vastuu tilanteesta ei saa jäädä liikaa urheilujärjestöjen, kuten Suomen Jääkiekkoliiton ja Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliitto IIHF:n varaan.

title: Q&A: What is the Brazil-led ‘deforestation roadmap’?
content:
• What is a deforestation ‘roadmap’?
  • What does the roadmap say about reducing deforestation?
  • Why did some countries not sign onto the roadmap at COP30?
  • What are the barriers to implementing a deforestation roadmap? 

    • On 3 November, the Brazilian presidency of the COP30 climate talks released its long-awaited “roadmap” on ending deforestation. 

    Ahead of the Belém summit, Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made a call for a “roadmap” to halt and reverse deforestation.

    Although this voluntary roadmap was outside the COP’s official agenda, it snowballed into a rallying point at the “Amazon” COP.

    By the end of the summit, 93 countries had signed on to the deforestation roadmap, committing to develop voluntary pathways to reverse forest loss and degradation by 2030. 

    The Brazilian presidency called on countries to describe what a pathway away from deforestation could look like, what challenges and support they needed.

    This call was answered by 18 countries and four negotiating blocs that offered their inputs on the roadmap, along with scores of NGOs, research centres and other groups.

title: Museum Shop Trends: Five Ideas to Test
content:
Museum shops can introduce visitors to local makers, extend an exhibition’s story and generate income for the institution. They also have to make practical retail decisions about stock, pricing, access and the time available to their teams.

A useful starting point is to choose one change that fits your museum and test it. Better product information, a small local-maker range or clearer online collection options may be more useful than an expensive new retail feature.

Here are five areas to consider when developing a museum shop, with examples and questions to help you decide what is worth trying.

Responsible sourcing starts with details: materials, packaging, manufacturing and the evidence behind the supplier’s claims. A museum shop can help customers understand those details, but it should avoid calling a product sustainable without explaining why.

The British Museum shop provides a concrete example. Its Great Wave foldable tote bag is described as being woven from 100% recycled polyester and is inspired by Hokusai’s print. The product page gives a material specification and a collection connection. That is more useful to a buyer than a broad environmental label.

title: From Documenting Local Vocabulary to Organizing Wikipedia Contests: Two Workshops at WikiCamp Morocco 2026
content:
From 18 to 21 October 2026, Wikimedia Morocco organized the fourth edition of WikiCamp Morocco in Marrakesh under the theme “From Contribution to Initiative: Building a Team of Organizers Together.”

The event brought together Wikimedia contributors from 16 Moroccan cities, with a programme focused on developing organizational skills, sharing technical knowledge, and preparing volunteers to lead Wikimedia activities in their communities.

During the camp, I facilitated two workshops addressing different aspects of Wikimedia participation: documenting Moroccan vocabulary and pronunciation using Lingua Libre, and organizing Wikipedia editing contests, from selecting articles to preparing and managing contest pages.

The first workshop, titled “A Word from My City” (كلمة من مدينتي), focused on documenting regional vocabulary in Moroccan Darija, including the pronunciation, meaning, and geographical usage of words and expressions.

Moroccan Darija varies considerably across regions. Some words are widely used in one city but rarely heard elsewhere, while others have different pronunciations or meanings depending on the speaker’s location.

title: Asuntokauppa digitalisoituu ympäri Suomen: sähköisten kauppojen osuus kasvoi kaikilla alueilla
content:
Digitaalinen asuntokauppa DIASin ja Tilastokeskuksen tietoihin perustuva alueellinen vertailu osoittaa digitaalisen asuntokaupan yleistyvän laajasti eri puolilla Suomea. Tammi–syyskuussa digitaalisen kaupanteon osuus kasvoi jokaisella Tilastokeskuksen erikseen tilastoimalla alueella viime vuoden samaan ajanjaksoon verrattuna. Eniten, 17 prosenttiyksikköä, osuus kasvoi Pohjois-Suomessa. Pääkaupunkiseudulla ja kehyskunnissa kasvu oli kummassakin noin 15 prosenttiyksikköä.

Alueiden välillä on kuitenkin yhä suuria eroja asuntokaupan digitalisoitumisessa. Korkeimmillaan digitaalisten kauppojen osuus kaikista alueellisista välittäjien tekemistä asunto-osakekaupoista on jo yli 80 prosenttia, kun taas joillakin alueilla vielä noin puolet välittäjien kaupoista syntyy pankin konttorissa ja puolet sähköisesti.

Tammi–syyskuun aikana digitaalisten asunto-osakekauppojen määrä kasvoi Suomessa edellisvuoteen nähden 9 prosenttia. Samaan aikaan välittäjien tekemien asunto-osakekauppojen määrä laski noin 11 prosenttia. Kokonaisuutena DIAS-kauppojen osuus välittäjien tekemistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista oli syyskuussa 71 prosenttia, kun se vuotta aiemmin oli 57 prosenttia.

title: Kasvatusalan ammattilaisilla hyvät mahdollisuudet edistää väestön liikkumista – koulutus ei vielä anna siihen riittäviä valmiuksia
content:
Valtaosa väestöstä ei täytä liikkumissuosituksia ja liikkuu terveytensä kannalta liian vähän. Väestön liikkumisen edistämiseksi tarvitaan mukaan kaikki hallinnonalat. Erityisesti mukaan tarvitaan koulutuspolitiikka, jotta kasvatus- ja opetusammattilaiset osaisivat omassa työssään edistää liikkumista ja liikuntaa.

Valtion liikuntaneuvoston tilaaman selvityksen mukaan liikkuminen on tunnistettavissa useimmissa tarkastelluissa kasvatusalan koulutuksissa, mutta liikkuminen muodostaa vain harvoin kaikille opiskelijoille yhteisen, koulutuksen eri osiin ulottuvan osaamisalueen. Liikkuminen keskittyy usein yksittäiseen opintojaksoon tai valinnaiseen kokonaisuuteen tai jää opetuksen käytännön toteutustavaksi.

Selvityksen kyselyyn vastanneet kasvatusalan ammattilaiset pitävät ammattialan roolia merkittävänä liikkumiseen ohjaamisessa. Vastaajat myös toivovat liikkumisen näkyvän tutkinnon tavoitteissa ja tai sisällöissä nykyistä enemmän. Kasvatusalan koulutuksissa on jo runsaasti sisältöjä ja tavoitteita, joihin liikkuminen voidaan luontevasti kiinnittää nykyistä vahvemmin.

title: Lucia Cerullo’s Elamite Metalworks, Part 2
content:
Dr. Lucia Cerullo is an archaeologist and art historian with a PhD in Asia, Africa, and the Mediterraneum from the University of Naples “L’Orientale”, in Italy. Her academic path began with a focus on Elamite epigraphy, explored in her Bachelor’s thesis on royal inscriptions from Persepolis. Over time, she developed a dual focus in archaeology and epigraphy, which she sees as essential in fully understanding ancient cultures. She has worked as an archaeologist in Italy, and held senior roles in fieldwork across Uzbekistan and Iran, including nearly seven years at the Iran National Museum in Tehran. Her expertise focuses on 1st Millenium BCE material culture, especially metal objects and pottery. 

What can we learn from studying these collections, and what kind of knowledge gap can we fill with that knowledge?

content:
Pohjois-Karjalan, Pohjois-Savon ja Etelä-Savon maaseutualueille suunnattu Itäkulmat-pilottihaku keräsi yhteensä 91 hakemusta. Niissä esitetään ratkaisuja siihen, miten taide, kulttuuri ja luovat alat voivat vahvistaa yhteisöllisyyttä, elinvoimaa ja yhteistyötä maaseutualueilla.

Kulttuuri ei ole vain sisältöä tai tapahtumia, vaan myös väline uusien yhteistyömallien rakentamiseen, yhteisöllisyyden vahvistamiseen ja alueiden vetovoiman lisäämiseen käytännön toiminnan kautta, kommentoi Itäkulmat-hankkeen projektipäällikkö Hannele Autti Pohjois-Karjalan maakuntaliitosta.

Valittujen yhteisöjen kanssa käynnistetään yhteinen kehittämisprosessi, jossa mukana ovat Itäkulmat-hankkeen asiantuntijat sekä kulttuurin ja luovien alojen ammattilaiset. Pilotit toteutetaan vuoden 2027 aikana.

title: Five projects awarded funding through Volt – a Nordic culture and language programme for young people
content:
The applications covered a wide range of artistic forms including film, literature, photography, sound-art, and poetry. The projects explored the concept of belonging in a variety of ways.

“The highest-scoring projects submitted some robust proposals and took a hands-on approach to exploring what it means to belong,” says Randi Samsonsen, chair of the expert group responsible for funding decisions.

“Another common feature of the projects awarded funding is that they create opportunities for the children and young people involved to meet in person, allowing ideas and experiences to emerge through real-life encounters. For the projects selected, the emphasis is on the quality of interaction, rather than simply the number of participants,” Samsonsen explains.

Nordic Lunch Stories is a youth-led environmental arts project bringing together 12–15-year-olds from Finland, Sweden, and Denmark. Through sound, storytelling, performing arts, and food culture, the young participants collaborate to create an artistic residency, a multilingual soundscape, and a public presentation exploring how we can live more sustainably in our day-to-day lives.

title: A New Search Engine Lets You Explore 4 Million Works of Art & Historical Photographs from Museums and Libraries Around the World
content: We live in an age when you can describe practically anything you want to see in words, then see it almost immediately. Nobody will ever have laid eyes upon that particular sight before — and quite possibly, nobody ever will again. There we have both the upside and the downside of artificial intelligence-powered image generation. A constant flow of visual, aural, or textual novelty offers stimulation, to put it mildly, but it inevitably comes to feel insubstantial. However complexly derived from the work of humanity it may be, it lacks a direct connection to that work. Not so the results delivered by Arkivism, a new search engine that responds to descriptions by drawing on a collection of more than four million pieces of real art and photography.

title: Beware a Balkan Chinese-Russian Cyber Danger
content:
When Bosnia and Herzegovina held general elections last month, it used biometric voter identification and ballot scanners — a reform widely praised for producing fast and accurate results. That’s a real achievement. But the region’s digital foundations remain fragile, and the region’s adversaries know it.

The Balkan chessboard remains checkered, torn between attraction to the European Union and to Russia, with China maneuvering for leverage. Bosnian nationalists, including separatist, pro-Russian Serbs, won the recent vote. But Serbs gave a pro-European student-led movement a clear majority in another October election, while Montenegro and Albania closed chapters in their EU accession talks. 

The cheapest way to shift the balance of power is to undermine trust in the ballot. For the region, cybersecurity is not a technical issue. It is a strategic one. Washington is waking up to the risk — but needs to increase its focus on digital dangers. The EU is already pressing for action but must also increase its scrutiny.

title: Google Summaries Aren't About AI, They're About Lock-In
content:
Whether they call it AI summaries, knowledge panels, or AMP, Google takes actions that are less about functionality and more about locking you into its own ecosystem. Knowing that makes it possible for all of us to choose better services than Google's, defeating their anticompetitive goal. In this case, as it is so often, knowledge is power.  

In the old days, when dinosaurs roamed the earth and getting online involved your computer making eldritch shrieking, Google was a website that took whatever you typed in and gave you a list of links that best matched what you were searching for. As it's grown beyond that, however, the core function of Google Search has moved from giving you the best answer to your query to a number of other things, most of them about making money for Google. 

This is obviously not a new observation. It's at the core of what EFF Special Advisor Cory Doctorow named "enshittification." But it's important to remember that whatever shiny new name or technology is wrapped around these tools, it's not about the wrapping, it's about the monetization.

title: Commission turns to artificial intelligence to write better laws
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission is now using artificial intelligence to draft new laws and simplify existing ones, it said in an annual review of progress on its ongoing simplification drive.

As part of a major plan to cut red tape and administrative costs for businesses, the EU is making deep reforms to how it creates and enforces rules on everything from tech, agriculture and migration to environmental protection and taxation.

To do that, the Commission is deploying new digital tools internally to “modernise” lawmaking. The tools aim to help its staff “identify similarities across legal acts, pointing at potential overlaps, inconsistencies or duplicates, as well as opportunities for simplification,” it said in an annual simplification report presented on Wednesday.

According to the document, the Commission is also beefing up legal training and staff to make sure new rules are not overly complex.

title: Thailand: Halt imminent forcible return of two Uyghur men to China
content:
Responding to reports that two Uyghur men recently moved to an Immigration Detention Centre in Thailand face imminent forcible deportation to China, Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnès Callamard said:

“Thai authorities must immediately halt any plans to forcibly return these two Uyghur men to China, where they face a real risk of torture, arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. Thailand must not repeat last year’s unlawful deportation of 40 Uyghurs, who were forced back to danger in China.

“These two men fled persecution only to spend more than a decade detained in Thailand. Amnesty International has documented crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim ethnic groups in Xinjiang. Returning them would expose them to the abuses they sought to escape.

“Both men have previously made clear to their legal representatives that they fear for their lives if returned to China and do not consent to being sent back. Thai authorities must now allow them access to a lawyer of their choice and, together with the international community, urgently find a safe and voluntary third-country solution for them and the other Uyghurs still detained in Thailand.

title: "The Earth Shook Last Night": Talarico Wins Senate, Hinojosa Becomes First Latina Governor in Texas
content:
Texas Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance in the state, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. They are also poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. The Republican governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, lost his bid for a fourth term to Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa, who defeated him by nearly 700,000 votes. She will be Texas’s first Latina governor. And James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since 1993.

“We’re celebrating these wonderful candidates who won office, and we’re also starting to think about what it means to hold power,” says Mike Siegel, a city council member from Austin, Texas, who founded Ground Game Texas, a statewide voter turnout organization. “We need to start thinking very quickly about how we will protect public education, how we will stop data centers and the encroachment of AI on our society, how we will protect public schools, how we stop collaboration with ICE.”

title: Tracing the recruitment trap behind Russia’s war
content:
No justice for Bangladeshi workers who are recruited into Russia’s war

Originally published on Global Voices

War-wounded Bangladeshis in Russia plead to return home. Screenshot from a YouTube report by Ekhon TV. Fair use.

Maksudur Rahman was 31 when a labor recruiter arrived in his hometown in Lakshmipur district, southeastern Bangladesh, with a job offer: becoming a janitor in Russia. Nearly every family in the district has someone working overseas, so the pitch landed. According to an international investigation, he borrowed money and paid the broker BDT 1.2 million (about USD 9,800). For a household like his, that is a fortune, but the promised wages made the debt look manageable. He signed up and flew out.

title: Amirhossein Mousavi Sentenced to Death and Imprisonment
content:
According to HRANA, Amirhossein Mousavi has been sentenced to imprisonment and death.

A source close to Mousavi’s family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “Today, Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the verdict issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, was communicated to Mr. Mousavi. title: COP31: Human Rights Critical for Climate Action
content:
(Istanbul) – Governments participating in the 31st annual United Nations climate change conference (COP31) should urgently act to protect the rights of communities displaced by the climate crisis and ensure that civil society groups can participate in the negotiations, Human Rights Watch said today. 

COP31 will take place in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9 to 20, 2026, under the shared presidency of Türkiye and Australia, on behalf of the Pacific Region. Negotiating countries and international climate funds should ensure that the needs of communities on the front lines of climate impacts and fencelines of fossil fuel extraction are driving the discussions, not corporate interests. 

“Intensifying climate impacts are already uprooting entire communities, yet those bearing these consequences are too often excluded from the decisions that determine their futures,” said Maria Laura Canineu, deputy environment director at Human Rights Watch. “Governments in Antalya should put affected communities at the center of climate action by ensuring that adaptation finance flows to displaced communities and to defending the space for civil society to hold government leaders accountable.”

title: What do Taylor Swift and Giorgia Meloni have in common?
content: Taylor Swift, a billionaire pop empress, and Giorgia Meloni, the far-right Italian prime minister, aren't often mentioned in the same breath. But they're caught in a similar battle, both trying to find new ways to fight an army of AI deepfakes by filing for EU trademarks to protect their voices. Swift's company, TAS Rights Management LLC, wants to register her saying “Hey, it's Taylor Swift”, according to a 6 October filing at the EU Intellectual Property Office. Meloni filed on 5 October to register herself saying “Io sono Giorgia Meloni.” While you can't trademark someone's voice as a whole, these trademarks would give them the exclusive right to their voice saying those words. That could technically stop anyone else from using the voice for a deepfake. Infringing a trademark risks lawsuits and claims for financial damage. It might also be easier to get tech platforms to quickly remove trademark-infringing content. Swift already filed for a US trademark for her voice earlier this year. The actor Matthew McConaughey secured trademarks for his voice last year, including for the phrase “alright, alright, alright” from the film Dazed and Confused. Lionel Richie and the Backstreet

title: ‘There Is One Fight’: American Voters Reject Tech Oligarchy
content:
Last month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Politico that “we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology,” referring to ChatGPT users dying, people losing their jobs to AI, and the other negative externalities we have seen from AI. 

Altman wasn’t running for office Tuesday. But this worldview—that the masses must shut up and suffer while oligarchs centralize power, self-deal, spend wildly to capture the political process, and automate away human endeavors so they can amass yet more wealth—was wholly repudiated in Tuesday’s election as people in Red States, Blue States, and Purple States rejected the cruelty, corruption, and depravity economy we’ve seen over the last few years. They are tired of kleptocracy.

title: US Sentences Venezuelan National to 12 Years for Laundering Over $1 Billion
content:
A U.S. district court sentenced a 60-year-old Venezuelan national Jorge Figueira to 12 years in prison and ordered him to surrender $1 billion for running a money laundering network tied to drug trafficking organizations, according to a Tuesday statement.

Investigators found that Figueira's operation moved over $1 billion through a single cryptocurrency wallet and various financial accounts. The network funneled the illicit funds into and out of the U.S. using shell companies, traditional bank accounts, and cryptocurrency exchanges, directing outbound money to individuals and businesses worldwide, including in Colombia, China, Panama, and Mexico.

title: Vermont Has Spent Nearly a Billion Dollars to Clean Up Lake Champlain. But the Green Slime Keeps Coming Back.
content:
On the last day of August, Jeff van den Noort spotted thick swirls of neon green film coating the water just steps from his home in Vermont. He waded in up to his ankles and dipped a jar to get a sample of the scum.

It wasn’t the first time he’d seen the slime. Since his parents bought the house on an island in Lake Champlain in 1966, van den Noort has spent part of nearly every summer in this quiet spot. Back then, the lake was clear.

But he began to witness the water’s deterioration as he grew older, especially after he moved into the home full time in 2010 to care for his ailing mother. That day in late August was the worst he’d seen all summer. 

Later that week, van den Noort grabbed a bucket, a few Mason jars and a smartphone and got into his rusty Saab. He drove past the boat launches, frozen-in-time general stores and windswept pastures of the lake’s islands in northern Vermont and stopped at four other spots along the shore. Each time, he collected some murky water, gauged how thick the muck was, took a few photos and jotted down the weather conditions. He then uploaded his report to an online database.

title: Speaking in a second language may shift your moral compass – but it can’t overpower it
content:
In today’s interconnected world, millions of people move between two or more languages every day. They may negotiate at work in one language, speak with family in another, and follow news, entertainment and social media across several others.

Using multiple languages can deeply change the way a person sees the world. Research has suggested that thinking and speaking in different languages can fundamentally shift the way we reason and behave, and even change our morality.

Some studies have suggested that using a second language encourages people to make more rational, utilitarian choices, meaning they prioritise the greatest good for the greatest number of people. This is possibly because moral dilemmas feel less emotionally charged when processed in a second language.

But the effect is not cut and dried – other studies have found little or no such effect.

One reason for these mixed findings is that language is only one part of the story. People do not enter a dilemma as a blank slate – they also bring values, past experiences, and sense of self. To date, most research has focused primarily on which language people use, while paying less attention to the person making the decision.

title: ‘Epic’ blue wave helps Democrats take Congress in overwhelming rebuke to President Trump
content:
Voters turned out in massive numbers on Election Day to hand Democrats control of Congress, in a sweeping snub of President Donald Trump and Republicans. Democrats won several statewide races in places long considered GOP bastions, including races that were considered insurmountable even weeks ago.

Democrats took control of the House and Senate, flipping Senate seats in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Kansas and Ohio. The results reflected broad dissatisfaction across the country with Trump, his agenda and the candidates he had endorsed.

The Conversation’s senior politics editor, Alfonso Serrano, spoke on election night with Charlie Hunt, a scholar at Boise State University who studies Congress and elections.

It was obviously a strong showing for Democrats on Election Day, something that was even evident in the margin of some Democratic losses. What does it tell you, for example, that democratic socialist Angie Nixon fought a competitive race for the Senate in Florida?

title: Veripankki kyberhyökkäyksen kohteena Ranskassa – huomattiin ajoissa
content:
Ranskassa on tehty kyberhyökkäys valtiolliseen veripankkiin ja alueelliseen pankkiin. Cyber Security News -verkkosivuston mukaan EFS-veripankin jäähdytyslaitteistoja valvovaan Coolworld-yritykseen hyökättiin tiistain vastaisena yönä.

Hyökkäyksen vuoksi jäädytetyn veriplasman lämpötila säiliöissä oli vaarassa nousta liian korkeaksi. Hyökkäyksessä säiliöiden lämpötila, jonka tulisi olla 30 pakkasastetta, asetettiin nousemaan peräti 110 asteeseen.

Veripankin ilmoituksen mukaan hyökkäys huomattiin kuitenkin ajoissa, eikä vahinkoa tapahtunut.

Myös ranskalainen Credit Mutuel Arkea -pankki ilmoitti kyberhyökkäyksestä. Uutistietojen mukaan pankista tehtiin petollisia tilisiirtoja noin 118 miljoonan arvosta. Pankki ei ole kertonut, paljonko se menetti rahaa mutta on vakuuttanut, ettei asiakkaille koidu vahinkoa.

Pankki ei kertonut, koska hyökkäys tehtiin tai kenen se arvelee olevan hyökkäyksen takana.

title: Yhdysvaltain välivaalit antavat toivoa, myös ilmastolle
content:
Yhdysvaltain välivaalit antavat maailmalle jotakin, mistä on viime aikoina ollut puutetta: toivoa. Demokraatit voittivat sekä edustajainhuonee että senaatin, ja tulos on selvä tappio presidentti Donald Trumpin johtamalle republikaanipuolueelle.

Trump onnitteli demokraatteja ja ilmoitti olevansa valmis yhteistyöhön. Samalla hän uhkasi käyttää veto-oikeuttaan demokraattien lakiesityksiä vastaan pakottaakseen nämä neuvottelupöytään. Kongressin enemmistön vaihtuminen vaikeuttaa joka tapauksessa Trumpin mahdollisuuksia toteuttaa politiikkaansa presidenttikauden jäljellä olevina kahtena vuotena.

Äänestäjät ovat vaihtaneet suuntaa muuallakin. Puolassa kansallismielinen Laki ja oikeus -puolue oli vallassa kahdeksan vuotta mutta menetti vuoden 2023 vaaleissa enemmistönsä, vaikka sen hallitsema valtiollinen televisio väitti vielä kaksi päivää vaalien jälkeen puolueen voittaneen. Unkarissa Viktor Orbánin 16 vuotta jatkunut valtakausi päättyi tänä keväänä opposition vaalivoittoon. Molemmissa maissa vallanpitäjät olivat pyrkineet vahvistamaan asemaansa myös median ja yhteiskunnallisten instituutioiden kautta. Siitä huolimatta oppositio onnistui voittamaan vaalit.

title: Q&A: What is in the global ‘roadmap’ for transitioning away from fossil fuels?
content:
• Why has Brazil produced a fossil-fuel ‘roadmap’?
  • What does the fossil-fuel roadmap say?
  • How will the fossil-fuel roadmap be discussed at COP31?

    • Transitioning away from fossil fuels is “urgent, inevitable and, yet, possible”, according to a first-of-its-kind global “roadmap” produced by Brazil.

    The host of last year’s climate summit, COP30, has set out a voluntary plan for how countries can move away from coal, oil and gas.

    The roadmap says there is no “one-size-fits-all” approach to transitioning away from fossil fuels and asks countries to “diagnose” their own “readiness” to start the process.

    After mapping out their specific circumstances, countries should then pursue “tailored levers” to take action, according to the roadmap.

    These efforts should culminate by 2033, it says – 10 years on from when the COP28 climate summit in Dubai called on all countries to contribute to a global transition away from fossil fuels.

    Below, Carbon Brief examines what the roadmap says and how it could influence debates about fossil fuels at the upcoming COP31 climate summit, which begins next week in Turkey.

title: From Figma to a Working Prototype: Building Wikimedia Morocco’s Website with OFPPT Students in Two Days
content:
On 22–23 October 2026, 20 students from Morocco’s Office of Vocational Training and Employment Promotion (OFPPT) joined Wikimedia Morocco contributors at ISTA Taddart in Agadir for a two-day Mini-Hackathon. Participants were divided into four teams, each working on a technical project related to Wikimedia.

I mentored a team of five students responsible for developing a prototype of Wikimedia Morocco’s official website. Our objective was to build a platform that could present the user group’s activities, projects, and resources while providing a maintainable foundation for future development.

Rather than focusing exclusively on delivering a set of web pages, we approached the hackathon as a complete software development exercise, covering requirements analysis, interface design, implementation, integration, testing, and project presentation.

We began on 22 October by identifying the website’s main requirements and defining its core structure.

Our priorities were to organize information clearly, improve access to Wikimedia Morocco’s activities and resources, and provide a responsive experience across desktop and mobile devices.

title: Kaaos kulisseissa tuo farssin mestariteoksen Hämeenlinnaan!
content:
Mitä tapahtuu, kun ei aivan parhaassa vedossa olevalla näyttelijäseurueella on alle vuorokausi aikaa ensi-iltaan - ja rakkaussuhteet, mustasukkaisuus, unohtuneet vuorosanat ja väärinkäsitykset takaavat, ettei mikään suju käsikirjoituksen mukaan? Michael Fraynin maailmankuulu farssikomedia Kaaos kulisseissa vie katsojat teatterin kulissien taakse, missä näyttämön tapahtumat ovat vasta alkua todelliselle katastrofille. Hämeenlinnan Teatterin syksyn neljännessä ensi-illassa nähdään yhdeksän näyttelijää, ja mukana on myös ensimmäistä kertaa Hämeenlinnan Teatterissa vieraileva Tom Lindholm.

Tästä syntyy Kaaos kulisseissa (Noises Off), brittiläisen Michael Fraynin rakastettu farssikomedia, jota on esitetty ympäri maailmaa. Teoksen erityisyys piilee sen nerokkaassa rakenteessa: yleisö pääsee seuraamaan kahta näytelmää samanaikaisesti. Ensin nähdään, kuinka näyttelijäseurue yrittää harjoitella ja myöhemmin esittää Ei ketään kotona -nimistä farssia. Samalla päästään kurkistamaan kulissien taakse, missä ihmissuhteet ja kulloinkin vallitsevat olosuhteet ja yhä kaoottisemmiksi muuttuvat tilanteet uhkaavat kaataa koko esityksen.

title: Abdul El-Sayed Becomes First Muslim Senator as Democrats Rout GOP Across the U.S. in Rebuke to Trump
content:
In a stunning repudiation of President Trump, Democrats regained control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, flipping seven Senate seats: Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. Meanwhile, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican Congressmember Mike Rogers for an open Senate seat in Michigan with over 52% of the vote. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, tackling economic inequality and getting big money out of politics — as well as ending military aid to Israel. He is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. El-Sayed faced vitriolic, Islamaphobic attacks by top Republicans throughout the campaign.

“Last night wasn’t just about Dr. Abdulrahman being a Muslim, winning and going to the United States Senate,” says Palestinian American organizer and author Linda Sarsour, who has been campaigning for El-Sayed. “It demonstrated that progressives can win in states like Michigan” and that “we can win on standing up for the human rights of the Palestinian people.”

title: Revolutionary Court in Kerman Sentences Three Baha’i Citizens to Eight Years in Prison Each
content:
According to HRANA, citing IranWire, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour have been sentenced to a combined 24 years in prison.

According to the report, on October 31, 2026, Branch 5 of the Revolutionary Court of Kerman issued verdicts against these Baha’i citizens on charges including “membership in a group,” “assembly and collusion,” and “propaganda against the regime.” Under the rulings, Venus Hosseini-Nejad, Shakila Ghasemi, and Adib Shahbazpour were each sentenced to eight years in prison.

In connection with the same case, two other Baha’i citizens, Peyvand Naeimi and Borna Naeimi, have also been sentenced to a combined total of more than 24 years in prison.

Shakila Ghasemi was released from Kerman Prison on bail on August 15, 2026. She had previously been arrested by security forces at her residence in Kerman on February 2, 2026.

Adib Shahbazpour was arrested by security forces on January 18, 2026, in connection with nationwide protests, while Venus Hosseini-Nejad was arrested on January 15 of the same year. Both were subsequently released on bail.

title: Burkina Faso: Islamist Armed Group Targets Civilians
content:
(Nairobi) – An Al-Qaeda-linked armed group killed at least 27 civilians in two attacks in Burkina Faso’s northern Yatenga province in September 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. These attacks violated international humanitarian law and are apparent war crimes.

On September 1, the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, or JNIM) attacked a gold mining site in Soubo, Ouahigouya district, killing 24 civilians, injuring at least 20 others, and burning property. On September 5, three civilians on a motorcycle, including a child, were killed by an explosive weapon on a dirt track near Mera village, also in Ouahigouya district. Local residents believe JNIM forces had planted an improvised explosive device (IED).

“The JNIM armed group’s relentless, unlawful attacks put civilians across Burkina Faso at grave risk,” said Ilaria Allegrozzi, senior Sahel researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities should urgently strengthen protection for threatened communities, investigate abuses, and fairly prosecute those responsible.”

title: Funding to help poorer countries cope with climate crisis has stalled, says UN
content:
Report reveals financial support promised by rich nations for adaptation measures is well behind the pace that is needed

Flows of money to help poor countries cope with the climate crisis have been flat or falling since 2022, despite growing impacts from extreme weather and warnings from scientists that global heating may be accelerating.

A new UN report has revealed that financial support for adaptation – which includes measures such as stronger infrastructure, early warning systems, flood protection and drought-resilient irrigation – is woefully short of what is needed and far behind even the inadequate promises that rich countries signed up to in 2021 in recognition of their far greater responsibility for the crisis.

title: Domestic abuse leaves receipts
content: Your bank statement says a lot about your lifestyle. For women, it could also provide early hints of domestic abuse, according to a recent Nature paper. Using data from Lloyds, the UK's largest retail bank, the study found certain banking patterns in domestic abuse victims' statements as early as seven years before they disclosed their situation. The authors compared more than 5,000 women who had told their bank they were experiencing abuse with over 15,600 customers who had not. Women who disclosed abuse were more likely to have missed a payment, and had lower credit scores. They were also more likely to receive welfare benefits, and their savings were £3,500 lower on average. Their spending patterns also differed: they spent less on self-care, such as the dentist, optician, or sports, and more on alcohol – possibly as a coping strategy, the authors noted. They also spent more on taxis and legal fees. They withdrew cash and changed PIN numbers and address more often, which the authors argue could hint at an abuser taking control of their finances, but also victims regaining it after leaving. title: Donald Trump Jr. Discussed Deals With Russian Businessman Close to Putin’s Personal Security Chief, Two Sources Say
content:
Donald Trump Jr. makes no secret of his relationship with Kremlin-linked businessman Umar Kremlev.

In 2025, the two men appeared together on stage in Istanbul at a meeting of the International Boxing Association, of which Kremlev is president. “I am proud to call Umar not only a leader but a friend,” Trump Jr. said.

And earlier this year, after ProPublica revealed that Kremlev had rented out a private island for Trump Jr.’s wedding, his new wife posted on Instagram that this had been “an extraordinarily generous” gift from “our dear friend Umar.”

But now, as reported by OCCRP’s Russian partner Important Stories, there may be more than friendship on the agenda. Two sources independently told the outlet’s reporters that Kremlev told them he and Trump Jr. had met in Kazakhstan to discuss business deals earlier this year.

Kremlev referred to those encounters as “business meetings,” they said. Both sources were quoted anonymously to ensure their safety.

title: Do You Live Near Lake Champlain? Help Seven Days and ProPublica Investigate Algae Blooms.
content:
Despite being an iconic part of Vermont’s landscape and a large source of the state’s drinking water, Lake Champlain has been polluted for decades. Phosphorus runoff from farm fields, rural roads, parking lots, stormwater drains and wastewater treatment plants flows into the lake, fueling algae blooms that frequently choke its bays and shorelines.

Vermont is halfway through a 20-year effort to clean up the lake. In 2016, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency established new, stricter requirements for reducing phosphorus runoff that the state must meet by 2036. But more than a decade in, after spending nearly a billion dollars, the state is lagging behind. Water quality has not improved dramatically, and in some parts of the lake, it is getting worse. This past summer algae blooms shut down swimming at public beaches in St. Albans Bay in the northeast part of the lake.

title: Donald Trump’s Republicans suffer landslide defeat – what this means for the world
content:
Donald Trump’s Republican Party has received a stunning rebuke in the US midterm elections. Republicans went into the evening hoping that the polls might be wrong and that they could at least cling on to control of the Senate. But by midnight in Washington, the GOP was staring down what looked like its worst defeat in 50 years.

Republican losses were not just confined to the type of swing districts that parties usually worry about on election night. The scale of the losses was staggering. They lost Senate seats in deep red states such as Texas and South Carolina. They lost districts they had gerrymandered and in which they were supposed to be unbeatable. They lost seats that even the sharpest analysts thought were safe.

Why? For months, surveys have shown that voters are fed up with high prices, with the war in Iran, and with what is increasingly being talked about as the Trump administration’s corruption. A president who was narrowly elected on the promise of a steady economic hand instead spent two years pursuing an extreme ideological agenda favoured only by a minority of Americans. He ignored what voters were saying, and now they have delivered a harsh verdict.

title: CB Live: Carbon Brief’s team at COP17 on the nature talks’ key outcomes
content:
Following this year’s UN COP17 biodiversity conference, Carbon Brief’s journalists hosted a livestream to explain what happened at the summit.

Carbon Brief’s Orla Dwyer and Aruna Chandrasekhar have been on the ground in Yerevan, Armenia, over the past two weeks, covering the negotiations.

They were joined on the livestream by associate editors Dr Giuliana Viglione and Daisy Dunne, who were following the talks from Washington DC and London, respectively.

Carbon Brief has also published its 10,000-word explainer of COP17, which lays out the key outcomes in detail.

Membership

Orla and Aruna kicked off the livestream by explaining the biggest issues at the event, including biodiversity finance and the first “global review” of progress towards reversing nature loss.

The four journalists then took live questions from the audience in an “ask me anything” format, covering issues such as “nature-harming subsidies”, marine biodiversity and the status of the Cali fund, which is meant to raise private-sector finance.

A recording of the webinar (below) is now available to watch on YouTube.

What happens when Wikimedia communities from India and Ukraine come together to explore and collect each other’s heritage? Heritage Across Borders turned this idea into a diverse and multilingual campaign, bringing contributors together from 15 to 24 August 2026, around both countries’ Independence Days.

The core objective was simple: discover another culture, document its heritage on wiki, and make that knowledge available in more languages. To make this objective a reality, Wikimedians from India worked on documenting Ukrainian heritage, while the Ukrainian community contributed to articles about Indian cultural heritage.

title: Lähitulevaisuudessa syöpähoito voidaan räätälöidä jokaisen yksilöllisen immuunipuolustuksen mukaan, tutkija uskoo
content:
With an estimated 1.8 million mortalities per year, lung cancer is the deadliest cancer in the world. It also affects young people and people who have never smoked. Typically, this cancer is detected after it has already spread. 

Assistant Professor Heidi Haikala’s research focuses on cancer immunity, or the ability of the body’s defence system to identify and destroy cancer cells, as well as cancer drug resistance and precision cancer therapies.  A key question is why cancer immunotherapies, or drugs that activate the patient’s immune system against cancer, respond in different ways in different people: some patients respond effectively, which means that the drug is working, while in others the same drug’s effectiveness is poor or non-existent. 

“Practically speaking, cancer is a failure of the human immune system. In the study of lung cancer drug resistance, we focus primarily on the whole body’s immune system. This has been a groundbreaking research avenue in lung cancer as well as many other cancers. We now have the appropriate tools at last,” Haikala says.

title: WAM Reopens with New Galleries for Contemporary Art
content:
The exhibition Web of Wyrd features eight works from the 2020s, presented as large-scale projections and photographic prints. Ratté’s visually immersive works reflect her interest in science fiction, contemporary spirituality and animism. As part of the opening programme, Ratté’s work Archipels will be projected onto the museum’s façade daily from 17.00 to 19.00, from November through January. title: Retired Teacher Ali Ahmadi Beaten at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz
content:
According to HRANA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher from Nurabad Mamasani, was beaten by an official at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz.

A source close to Ahmadi’s family confirmed the incident to HRANA, stating: “On Sunday, November 1, Mr. Ahmadi was beaten by a prison official for unknown reasons while following up on medical treatment for his eye condition, despite having authorization to see a doctor. As a result, he sustained injuries to his head, face, nose, and back.”

The source further added: “In addition to his eye problems and a history of two surgical procedures involving his eye and prostate, Mr. Ahmadi also suffers from heart and kidney diseases. Nevertheless, prison authorities continue to prevent his transfer to medical facilities outside the prison.”

Previously, the Fars Teachers’ Trade Association reported that Ahmadi suffers from heart and kidney diseases. Furthermore, on September 1, 2026, despite a physician’s determination that he required medical care at facilities outside the prison, prison authorities, fully aware of his medical condition, prevented his transfer to a medical center.
snippet: According to HRANA, on Sunday, November 1, 2026, Ali Ahmadi, a retired teacher from Nurabad Mamasani, was beaten by an official at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz.

title: Bangladesh: Academics Allegedly Targeted for Supporting Hasina
content:
(London) – Scores of academics and students at public universities in Bangladesh have been arbitrarily punished because of their alleged affiliation with former ruler Sheikh Hasina and her Awami League party, Human Rights Watch said today.

Any action to punish persons for their peaceful beliefs or without ensuring due process would violate the rights to freedom of expression and association protected under international human rights law and reproduce abusive attempts under previous administrations to control political opinion and expression at Bangladesh’s public universities.

“Bangladesh has a long history of political debate in its universities, and only autocrats should fear such discourse, not a government formed following student protests,” said Meenakshi Ganguly, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Bangladesh needs to turn the page on the repression of the past, not repeat it whenever the ruling and opposition parties trade places.”
