title: Potsdam to host new Europa Nostra Heritage Hub with a focus on climate resilience, civic engagement and youth capacity-building
content:
The State Capital City of Potsdam has entered into a strategic partnership with Europa Nostra, the leading European heritage civil society organisation. On 29 October 2026, a Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Potsdam was signed at the Old Town Hall by Potsdam’s Lord Mayor Noosha Aubel, the Secretary-General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the President of Europa Nostra Germany, Dr. Uwe Koch. From 2027 onwards, the Hub in Potsdam will prioritise climate-resilient cultural heritage management, civic engagement and, above all, capacity-building for young people.

The new Hub brings together Potsdam’s local expertise and Europa Nostra’s transnational network. The Palaces and Parks of Potsdam, which are inscribed on UNESCO’s World Heritage List, and the city itself serve as a real-world laboratory for the conservation of cultural landscapes in the context of climate change. To this end, close collaboration with local institutions, such as the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) and the Research Centre Sanssouci (RECS), is foreseen.

title: Instituuttiverkoston ensimmäinen yhteinen vaikuttavuusarviointi on valmistunut
content:
Vuonna 2025 käyttöön otettu vaikuttavuusarviointi kokoaa yhteen tietoa verkoston toiminnan vaikutuksista. Arvioinnin tulokset perustuvat kyselyihin, joihin ovat vastanneet instituuttien kanssa työskentelevät taiteilijat, tutkijat ja muut asiantuntijat sekä instituuttien paikalliset yhteistyöorganisaatiot.

Vaikuttavuusarviointi tukee instituuttiverkoston yhteistä tavoitetta edistää kestävää kansainvälisyyttä. Tulokset kertovat instituuttien merkityksestä kansainvälisten verkostojen, osaamisen ja uusien ammatillisten mahdollisuuksien rakentajina.

Vaikuttavuuden arvioinnin teoreettisena viitekehyksenä on muutosteoria (Theory of Change). Instituuttien toiminnan vaikuttavuutta arvioidaan suhteessa siihen, missä määrin toiminnan kautta onnistutaan saavuttamaan niitä vaikutuksia, jotka verkosto on määritellyt toiminnan tavoitteeksi. Arviointimallin suunnitteluprosessista ja asetetuista tavoitteista voi lukea lisää täältä.

Vuoden 2025 arviointi perustuu instituuttien valitsemiin merkittävimpiin toimintoihin ja hankkeisiin.

title: An Agora only exists when people show up
content:
On the morning of 29 October, two weeks after the Irish Presidency of the Council of the EU presented a negotiation box proposing a 30% cut to AgoraEU, a wave of pink energy and joyful anger stormed Schuman Square, reclaiming it as what an agora should be: a space for people to gather and speak up.

AgoraEU is the future EU funding programme for culture, media and civil society, and the proposal to cut it by almost a third comes at a time when its share of the EU budget already amounts to just a tiny fraction of the whole. 

Cutting AgoraEU means fewer books, films and performances, fewer independent investigations, and less support for the people and organisations defending our rights. In short, it means less space for the voices, stories and ideas that bring our democracies to life. 

In response to this dreadful scenario, together with our partners and friends at Civil Society Europe, European Civic Forum, the European Federation of Journalists, and in the Future of Europe cohort, we called on the cultural, media and civil society sectors to stand up for AgoraEU. 

And we did. Marvelously, and in full pink.

title: Lönnemoskogenin ennallistamistalkoot ‒ luonnon elpymiseksi, elämänvaalijan muistoksi
content:
Lokakuussa 2024 metsänpuolustajia ja kohtuusliikettä kohtasi mittaamaton menetys. Aktivisti, omavaraisviljelijä ja elämänvaalija Eeva-Stiina Lönnemo menehtyi äkillisen ja kiivaan sairauden heikentämänä. Kaipaamaan jäivät lukemattomat ystävät, sukulaiset, toverit, naapurit sekä Eeva-Stiinan elämänkumppani ja puoliso Paula Lönnemo.

Jo ennen sairastumistaan Eeva‑Stiina toivoi, että hänen muistokseen kerätään lahjoituksia Luonnonperintösäätiölle metsien suojeluun. Kuoleman jälkeen Paula ja Meidän metsämme -kansalaisliike toteuttivat toiveen. Keräys Eeva-Stiinan muistometsän suojeluun tuotti päälle 27 000 euroa, joka kattoi suuren osan suojellun metsän hinnasta.

Muistometsäksi valikoitui noin 1,6 hehtaarin metsä Salon Perttelistä, aivan Eeva-Stiinan ja Paulan kotitalon, Lönnemon, vierestä. Metsä on Eeva-Stiinalle ja Paulalle rakas sieni- ja marja-apaja, rauhan ja ihmetyksen tyyssija. Se on uhanalaisten hömö- ja töyhtötiaisen, palokärjen, uhanalaisten sammalten ja monien muiden elollisten koti. Maallisen elämänsä viimeisen luontoretken Eeva-Stiina teki juuri tässä metsässä: vanamoiden helakoiden kellojen ihastelua vuoden 2024 valoisimpaan aikaan.

title: Watch 150 Classic Horror and Suspense Films Free Online: Nosferatu, The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Carnival of Souls, Night of the Living Dead & More
content: From roughly the mid-nineteen-fifties through the mid-nineteen-seventies, the availability of airtime on American television stations exceeded their capacity to fill it with high-quality original programming. This was especially true in the hours when relatively few viewers were awake to tune in, a condition that gave rise to the late-night movie show. Specializing in lesser Hollywood productions and the releases of by-then forgotten studios, these programs came to constitute home revival houses, and often eccentric ones. By its very nature, the repertoire of yesteryear’s “B movies” consisted mostly of genre pictures, and no genre proved as popular among this particular viewership as horror. Hence the eventual popularity of hosts like Vampira, Ghoulardi, and, later, the iconic Elvira, Mistress of the Dark.

title: Maksullinen kirjasto rapauttaisi lukutaitoa
content:
Valtiovarainministeriön tuoreessa virkapuheenvuorossa ehdotetaan kirjastokortin muuttamista maksulliseksi aikuisille. Kirjastolaissa määritelty tavoite väestön yhdenvertaisista mahdollisuuksista päästä osalliseksi sivistyksestä ja kulttuurista karkaisi tällä muutoksella kauas.

Suomalaiset ovat kirjastokansaa: meillä kirjastoja käytetään suhteessa väkilukuun enemmän kuin missään muualla Euroopassa. Maksullinen kirjastokortti saattaa valtiovarainministeriössä tuntua matalalla roikkuvalta hedelmältä, josta on tuloutettavissa kymmeniä miljoonia euroja.

Virkapuheenvuorossa mainitaan kirjastokortista maksua perivinä maina muun muassa Sveitsi ja Alankomaat. Näissä maissa kirjastojen käyttäjämäärät ovat kuitenkin huomattavasti Suomea pienemmät juuri maksullisuuden takia.

Lukutaidon heikkeneminen on tunnustettu kasvavaksi ongelmaksi ja uhaksi myös Suomen talouskasvulle. Yleinen kirjasto on ainoa julkinen instituutio, joka pitää huolta myös aikuisten lukutaidosta.

Haluammeko todella Suomen, jossa lukutaito heikkenee entisestään?

title: Data centre register proposal: what data centre providers in Finland should prepare for?
content:
The Finnish Government’s proposal (HE 282/2026 vp) on 29 October 2026 introduces mandatory notifications for data centres to the National Emergency Supply Agency (NESA, Fin. Huoltovarmuuskeskus). The aim is to contribute to a more comprehensive and anticipatory situational picture of the data centre investments, intended use and ownership of data centres, electricity demand and infrastructure needs in Finland. The proposed entry into force is 1 April 2027.

Broad scope and early notification. The register would cover planned, under-construction and operational data centres in Finland with planned or actual installed IT power demand of at least 0.5 MW. This refers to IT equipment threshold, not total grid connection capacity. Notifications would be due within 30 days of signing a grid connection agreement and, in all cases, before construction starts. Data centres within the scope of the act that have already concluded an electricity network agreement, are under construction, or are in operation would be required to submit a notification by 30 June 2027.

title: Rewriting Copyright Law for Generative AI Would Hurt Everyone
content:
In courts across the country, publishers and creators are suing large AI companies for training generative AI models on copyrighted works. It’s easy to see these cases as a David-and-Goliath showdown between authors and publishers fighting for a cut of Big Tech company profits. But this fight is actually much larger. It affects billions of people who aren’t represented in the case at all, including researchers, artists, activists, journalists, people with disabilities, and anyone who accesses and shares content online.   

That’s why EFF is stepping in to defend the public’s rights in these cases. Today, EFF filed an amicus brief in In re OpenAI, explaining how the court’s ruling on fair use could impact people worldwide. If fair use gets narrowed, it will impede work that benefits the public, like medical research and investigative journalism, and even limit access to privacy protection tools.

title: Towards Unlocking Spain’s Twentieth-Century Black Hole: Libraries and CEDRO in Dialogue at the LIBER 2026 Conference
content:
Blog post by Ana Ordás
See the Spanish coverage on FESABID’s website.

On 1 October, at the LIBER 2026 conference in Barcelona, FESABID, the Spanish Federation of Archives, Libraries, Museums and Documentation Associations, which serves as the national coordinator for Knowledge Rights 21 (KR21) in Spain, organised the roundtable: “Out-of-commerce works: dialogue between libraries and collective management.”

The session presented publicly, for the first time since late 2025, the state of play of the talks FESABID has held with CEDRO, the Spanish collective management organisation (CMO) for text-based works. The aim is to reach a framework licence agreement for out-of-commerce works.

The speakers were:

  • Antonio Martínez Bodi, from law firm Abogados de las Artes, legal adviser to FESABID in the negotiations;
  • Carolina Santamarina, from FESABID’s Intellectual Property Working Group; and,
  • Javier Díaz de Olarte, representing CEDRO.

title: 8 things we learned at the EU-Canada summit
content:
MONTREAL — Prime Minister Mark Carney wanted the landmark EU-Canada summit to be about much more than “nomenclature.” He got what he craved. 

Over a whirlwind 48 hours in Montreal, top officials from Brussels and Ottawa huddled to pursue agreements on critical minerals, super computers and defense cooperation.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa and Carney gathered as U.S. President Donald Trump continues to upend the global order and Chinese dominance of critical markets squeezes middle powers. 

Those challenges have pushed the EU and Canada into a rapidly developing partnership that eclipses anything attempted by Brussels with a non-member country since the bloc was formed. 

Here are all the key things POLITICO learned during the EU-Canada meetings. 

Initially reluctant, the Canadian prime minister came around by the end of the summit to endorse von der Leyen’s controversial label for the global alliance the EU and Canada are building. 

Carney set a six-month deadline to firm up the ground rules of what “associate membership” is, trialing an induction process that could be a model for other non-European countries.

title: Russia: Closure of Novaya Gazeta is a devastating loss for embattled media freedom
content:
Responding to the announcement that Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s last independent newspapers, will cease operations on 9 November, Denis Krivosheev, Amnesty International’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia Deputy Director, said:

“The closure of Novaya Gazeta is a devastating loss for everyone in Russia who turns to independent, investigative journalism to uncover the truth. This long-respected newspaper has withstood years of mounting state pressure, including criminal prosecutions, raids and attacks on staff members. Its journalists have been killed for doing their jobs. Its website has been blocked, its official registration cancelled and just last month, it was designated a “foreign agent.”

“The final blow has come with an eviction notice demanding that the newsroom vacate its premises, in addition to being cut off from online donations. While these measures were carried out by private actors, the authorities’ role is not in question. Their decades-long predatory campaign has resulted in the near complete annihilation of free media in Russia, and now, of its most celebrated and distinguished champion.

title: "Ungrounding": Eyal Weizman on Gaza Genocide & Israel's "Permanent Architecture of Control"
content:
We speak with Forensic Architecture’s Eyal Weizman about his new book, Ungrounding: The Architecture of Genocide, a meticulous investigation into Israel’s genocide in Gaza, the physical destruction of the territory and its impact on the Palestinian people.

Forensic Architecture was founded in 2010 as an interdisciplinary research group focused on investigating state violence and human rights violations. Since 2023, Forensic Architecture has focused on producing evidence for South Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice.

Weizman says “ungrounding” is “a kind of destruction that we have not seen anywhere else,” with Israeli bulldozers “terraforming” the landscape to erase all traces of Palestinian life. With thousands of bodies still unrecovered from under destroyed buildings, Israel’s flattening, extraction and reshaping of the rubble in Gaza is a continuation of its crimes, says Weizman.

“Israel is actively and against court order, against the order of the ICJ, destroying the evidence of the genocide that it has perpetrated,” he says.

title: Pakistan: Rights Lawyers Receive 10-Year Sentences
content:
(New York) – An anti-terrorism court in Pakistan imposed 10-year prison sentences on two human rights lawyers on October 29, 2026, in an escalation of the government’s crackdown on civil society, Human Rights Watch said today. Pakistani authorities should immediately quash the convictions, release Imaan Mazari-Hazir and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha, and cease criminal proceedings aimed at punishing human rights advocates.

The sentences were handed down following a trial held inside Adiala prison in Rawalpindi. The lawyers were accused of obstructing police at a road closure in Islamabad in October 2024. 

Instead of prosecuting them for a misdemeanor or common crime, the police charged them under Pakistan’s anti-terrorism act, which carries far greater penalties and a longer sentence. This was the second time in recent weeks that the two have been prosecuted in an apparent attempt to prevent them from carrying out their legal work.

title: ESSAY: The World to Come
content:
Jewish Mysticism and the Politics of Emancipation

By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 30 October  2026 (IDN) — What if the world we hope for is not somewhere in the distant future? What if, in some strange sense, it already exists? This is one possibility opened by the Zohar, the great masterpiece of Jewish mysticism.

Composed in medieval Spain and written largely as a mystical commentary on the Torah, the Zohar would seem an unlikely place to look for radical political ideas. It speaks of God, creation, the soul, good and evil, Scripture’s mysteries, and the hidden structure of reality. It is a profoundly religious work and, in many respects, a profoundly conservative one.

title: Puolalaisten Ukraina-vastaisuus kasvaa – vuonna 2027 retoriikka voi muuttua politiikaksi
content:
Antipatia Ukrainaa ja ukrainalaisia kohtaan kasvaa Puolassa. Oikeistoblokin kannatuksen kasvu osoittaa, että ensi vuoden parlamenttivaalit voivat koventaa Ukraina-vastaista retoriikkaa – ja pahimmillaan vähentää Ukrainan saamaa tukea. Jo nyt Ukraina-mielinen Tuskin hallitus on heikentänyt ukrainalaisten yhteiskunnallista asemaa julkisen paineen alla. Jännitteet kumpuavat historiasta ja politiikasta, mutta myös Venäjällä on oma lusikkansa sopassa. 

Täysimittainen sota Ukrainassa on jatkunut kohta jo viisi vuotta, eikä loppua näy. 

Puola on kuulunut Ukrainan suurimpiin tukijoihin aina siitä alkaen, kun Venäjä aloitti vuonna 2022 maassa laajamittaisen hyökkäyssotansa. Tällä hetkellä Puolassa asuu noin 1,5 miljoonaa ukrainalaista, joista noin 900 000 on saapunut pakolaisina.

Nyt Puolassa on kuitenkin tultu siihen pisteeseen, jossa enemmistö puolalaisista vastustaa ukrainalaisten vastaanottamista maahansa. 

Yleinen ilmapiiri on myös Puolan pääministeri Donald Tuskin julkilausuman mukaan kääntynyt Ukraina-vastaisemmaksi. Hänen mukaansa hyökkääjistä on tullut rohkeampia, koska he uskovat nauttivansa poliittista suojelua.

Suomen Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -verkoston 20-vuotisjuhlaseminaari kokosi perjantaina 30. lokakuuta Helsinkiin päättäjiä, asiantuntijoita ja kansalaisyhteiskunnan toimijoita keskustelemaan naisten oikeuksien, rauhan ja turvallisuuden tulevaisuudesta. Tilaisuudessa korostuivat huoli kansainvälisen sääntöpohjaisen järjestelmän heikkenemisestä sekä tarve puolustaa vuosikymmenten aikana saavutettua tasa-arvokehitystä.

Seminaarin avanneessa europarlamentaarikkojen paneelissa Ville Niinistö (vihr.) ja Jussi Saramo (vas.) keskustelivat Euroopan unionin roolista naisten oikeuksien ja rauhan edistäjänä. Keskustelun keskiöön nousivat tasa-arvon vastaisen liikehdinnän voimistuminen, kansainvälisen kehitysrahoituksen leikkaukset sekä naisten edelleen vähäinen osallistuminen rauhan- ja turvallisuuspoliittiseen päätöksentekoon. Paneelikeskustelua johdatteli Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuusverkoston ensimmäinen puheenjohtaja, työelämäprofessori, VTT Kaari Mattila.

title: The world needs the United Nations more than ever. It needs a new lease on life | Alex Rondos and Mark Medish
content:
We need neither ‘peace in our time’ nor ‘perpetual peace’ – but enough peace to keep civilization

To save the United Nations from the irrelevance in which it now wallows, the next secretary general will require the concerted backing of the few powers that govern the security council.

The paradox is that the great powers who created the institution in the 1940s and recently treat it with a cavalier cynicism are now the ones who need it most, as does the rest of the world.

title: Teaching under pressure
content: Teachers love teaching, according to the ones we spoke to in Sweden, Latvia, the UK, Bulgaria, Italy, and Germany. A 2024 European Commission report echoes that, saying nine out of 10 teachers across 23 countries were satisfied with the profession. But many teachers, including our interviewees, are frustrated by government budget cuts, low pay, declining working conditions, and too much paperwork. Only 15% of them feel they are valued by society, according to the Commission report. They're also often striving to hold the attention of children who have grown up with screens or missed some crucial school years during the Covid-19 pandemic. Teenagers' reading scores have fallen sharply since 2012, when smartphones started to become more common. Resentment and anger at how society is failing education – and how education risks failing kids – have fuelled protests and strikes across Europe, especially in France but also in Italy, Spain, Belgium, Greece Portugal, and Ireland. We wanted to find out: what do teachers think about their job and education? Beyond pay, they raised four issues. title: ‘Wake Up Call:’ Fanfiction Writers and Readers React to AO3 Outage
content:
In the wake of fanfiction repository Archive of Our Own (AO3) announcing a weeks-long security incident outage, readers and writers are reflecting on why the site is important to the fanfiction community, and how they’re coping with the downtime.  

On Thursday, the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the non-profit organization that runs AO3, posted that the site was down for maintenance, eventually updating to say the site restoration will take around two weeks, but could take up to a month. OTW confirmed in an updated status report Friday morning that this outage is due to a security incident. 

Some have speculated that the outage is a result of the PHP scramble this week that led to several sites going down to update their security, but AO3 doesn’t use PHP. An OTW representative told CNET: “I can let you know that this is not related to the PHP security issue as the Archive uses Ruby on Rails.”

title: Many EU countries have special anti-corruption agencies – but their very existence may signal systemic problems
content:
Experiences across EU countries shows that specialised anti-corruption agencies can play a crucial role in tackling political corruption, but their effectiveness depends on institutional independence and political will. While some countries have successfully prosecuted senior politicians, others continue to struggle with political interference, weakened law enforcement institutions and lengthy judicial proceedings. The European Public Prosecutor’s Office is becoming an increasingly important player in protecting EU funds and strengthening accountability.

Article:

  • Specialised anti-corruption agencies are not a solution in themselves. Their effectiveness depends on political independence, sufficient investigative powers and a functioning justice system.
  • The nine EU countries take different approaches to fighting corruption. Romania, Latvia and Lithuania have dedicated anti-corruption bodies, while Finland relies on cooperation between existing institutions.
  • Political interference remains a major obstacle. Recent institutional changes in countries such as Slovakia, Hungary, Poland and Bulgaria demonstrate how strongly anti-corruption efforts can depend on government priorities.

title: Russia introduces new laws to jail critics, but denies it holds any political prisoners
content: Every year on 30 October, the world marks the Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Political Repressions. Starting in 1974, when Soviet political prisoners coordinated a collective, one-day hunger strike in defiance of their captors and to call for official recognition of their status as political prisoners, the date today carries an uncomfortable irony in Russia. People are being imprisoned there on charges that rights groups say are false, yet the authorities refuse to recognise that political prisoners exist. Memorial, one of the main groups that kept the memory of Soviet repression alive and documented today’s cases, has been liquidated in Russia and branded “extremist.” It continues its activities in exile.

title: Alleged Turkish Crime Boss Assassinated Inside Spanish Hospital Room
content:
An alleged Turkish crime syndicate leader who survived an assassination attempt some two weeks earlier was fatally shot inside a Spanish hospital room early Thursday in a highly coordinated hit.

Catalonia’s regional police force, the Mossos d'Esquadra, announced they are investigating the fatal shooting of an admitted patient at a hospital in Tarragona. While police placed the case under a judicial secrecy order, a law enforcement source confirmed to OCCRP that the victim was Mekin Büyükdeniz, a member of the Ten Brothers criminal group.

According to Turkish media, the Küçükçekmece Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office formally named Büyükdeniz in prosecutorial filings as the operational leader of the so-called “10 Brothers” gang. In the organizational hierarchy documented in the prosecutor's investigation, the syndicate was identified as a family-centered armed network directed by the Büyükdeniz brothers.

title: Trump Has Tried to Exert More Control Over Elections. Here Are the Key Findings From Our Reporting.
content:
Ahead of next week’s midterm elections, President Donald Trump has systematically demolished institutional guardrails that prevented him from overturning the 2020 presidential election, ProPublica’s reporting has shown.

Trump has empowered his loyalists to try to transform the voting process. He launched an unprecedented — and largely unsuccessful — effort to find noncitizen voters. And he tried to restrict mail-in voting.

Our reporters have spent much of this year covering Trump’s efforts to exert more federal control over elections. Here are five takeaways from their reporting.

In April, Doug Bock Clark and Jen Fifield reported on Trump’s efforts to “take over” the midterm elections, detailing how the administration has discarded or diminished endeavors across the federal government to protect the voting process or block foreign interference. Those efforts have included cutting staff on election-related teams at federal law enforcement agencies and finding ways to exert greater federal control over voting.

title: Espionage Act: The zombie law haunting Halloween week
content:
Dear Friend of Press Freedom,

In the spirit of Halloween, we’re calling for an end to the Espionage Act — a zombie statute that keeps popping up to drag journalists and their sources into hell. More about the act and its latest victims below. Also, the Department of Homeland Security and cops are sabotaging public records requests, and a new coalition of veteran journalists is fighting back against censorship.

The Justice Department unsealed new Espionage Act charges against former FBI Director James Comey, accusing him of leaking national defense information to the press in 2016.

Comey has a strong argument that the prosecution violates the statute of limitations, but the problems with Espionage Act prosecutions go far beyond procedural technicalities. The 1917 law’s vagueness and overbreadth have long made it the government’s weapon of choice not only for political grudges but for prosecuting whistleblowers who share important news with the press and public. Comey’s own FBI led plenty of these investigations.

title: Tekijänoikeusbarometri 2026: Suomalaiset arvostavat ihmisten tekemää musiikkia myös tekoälyn aikakaudella
content:
Taloustutkimus Oy:n toteuttamasta Tekijänoikeusbarometrista käy ilmi, että peräti 81 % suomalaisista on sitä mieltä, ettei tunnetun taiteilijan tai esittäjän persoonallista tyyliä saa hyödyntää tekoälyn tuottamissa sisällöissä ilman lupaa ja korvausta. Lisäksi lähes kolme neljästä vastaajasta (74 %) katsoo, että tekoälyn kouluttamiseen käytetyistä teoksista tulee maksaa korvauksia tekijöille ja esittäjille.

Tekoälyn tuottamiin sisältöihin suhtaudutaan varauksellisesti. Vain 22 % vastaajista arvioi, että tekoälyn luomien sisältöjen tulisi olla samalla tavalla suojattuja ja korvauksen alaisia kuin ihmisten tekemien teosten. Kiinnostus tekoälyn tuottamaan sisältöön on vähäistä: vain kymmenesosa vastaajista kuluttaisi tekoälyn tuottamaa musiikkia yhtä mielellään kuin ihmisten tekemää.

Tulokset kertovat, että ihmisten luoma musiikki ja luova työ nähdään arvokkaana myös tekoälyn aikakaudella. Samalla ne viestivät vahvasta odotuksesta sille, että tekijöiden, esittäjien ja tuottajien oikeudet huomioidaan tekoälyn kehittämisessä ja hyödyntämisessä.

title: Where are the opportunities for closer Nordic cooperation in peace mediation?
content:
Deeper cooperation among the Nordic countries could strengthen peacemaking globally, said speakers at a high-level discussion organised by CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation and the Finnish delegation to the Nordic Council in Helsinki on 26 October.

Nordic peace mediation in a changing world order brought together Nordic parliamentarians, political actors and peacemaking experts during the 78th Session of the Nordic Council at the Parliament of Finland. Speakers called for “stronger political commitment” and “sustained investment in diplomacy and mediation”, alongside more effective use of the Nordic countries’ diverse and complementary expertise in peacemaking.

Last Monday’s event comes amid evolving geopolitical competition and realignment, with multilateral institutions under strain and international conflicts continuing to grow.

title: Toxic Feeds: Mapping the Digital Harms Ecosystem, Escalation and Accountability in Somalia
content: Somalia’s digital information environment has expanded faster than the institutions, norms, and laws needed to manage it. The country had 10.7 million internet users at the start of 2025, equivalent to 55.2 percent internet penetration, and 3.05 million social media user identities. Public platform figures should be interpreted carefully because advertising reach, registered identities, shared devices and actual users are not the same measure. Connectivity has created real benefits: civic voices can reach national audiences, diaspora communities remain closely connected to local debates, mobile money underpins everyday transactions, and remote education and information-sharing are more accessible than in previous decades. Yet the same infrastructure is also used to manufacture narratives, weaponise clan identity, silence women, intimidate journalists and accelerate conflict dynamics.

title: Elätkö sinäkin kiinalaista elämää?
content:
Oletko viime aikoina hiippaillut kotona pehmeissä tossuissa kuumaa omenavettä siemaillen? Silloin saatat olla kiinalaisen pehmeän vallan vaikutuspiirissä.

Ilmeisen orgaanisesti leviämään lähtenyt China­maxxing-ilmiö on varmasti Kiinan kommunistipuolueen mieleen. Siinä länsimaihin väsyneet länsimaiset Z-sukupolven edustajat ihailevat kiinalaista elämäntapaa ja teknologista kehitystä ja kertovat muuttuneensa kiinalaisiksi.

Kyseessä on pehmeä valta, jota levittävät etenkin amerikkalais-kiinalaiset sosiaalisen median vaikuttajat pehmeine tossuineen ja omenavesineen.

Pehmeän vallan konseptin lanseerasi amerikkalainen valtiotieteilijä Joseph Nye 1980-­luvulla. Se on valtion tapa saada toinen valtio tekemään, kuten se haluaa – ilman voimaa ja väkivaltaa. Etenkin kulttuuri nähdään pehmeänä valtana, mutta myös ulkopolitiikka ja poliittiset arvot voivat vaikuttaa vaivihkaa.

Esimerkiksi alasajettua USAIDia on pidetty Yhdysvalloille hyvin tehokkaana pehmeän vallan välineenä. Euroviisut ovat puolestaan olleet Israelille oiva pehmeän vallan areena.

Se, että Kiina ja kiinalaisuus nähdään etenkin Yhdysvalloissa tavoittelemisen arvoisina, on kommunistiselle puolueelle valtava voitto.

title: The Sediment Of Culture Shapes Political Order
content:
As a global journal of ideas, Noema receives feedback from readers all over the world that broadens our way of seeing and kindles the further iteration of our thinking. One recent case is a response by Carl Gay, an executive of the Cloudspago consultancy in Australia, to the Noema essay “When The Present Eats The Future: The Achilles Heel of Consumer Democracies.”

In that essay, I contrast post-Mao China’s capacity for reaching a consensus on long-term goals and determinedly implementing them over many years without a break in continuity with the increasing inability of consumer democracies to do so. The example I used in the context of climate change was how China set the goal decades ago of dominating green technology, especially electric vehicles and batteries, and has steadily achieved that objective, while most open societies of the West have sputtered behind. Its “whole dragon” approach brings the resources of the entire system to bear on the challenge at hand.

title: Massive sinkholes open up across Turkey as it struggles with drought and climate change
content:
Turkey’s central Anatolian plateau is one of the country’s most important agricultural regions, producing wheat, maize, sugar beet and other crops. Yet beneath its cultivated fields, the ground is becoming increasingly unstable.

Large sinkholes, some tens of metres wide and deep, have appeared across the Konya basin, swallowing farmland, and threatening nearby roads and settlements.

These collapses can occur suddenly, sometimes in fields that have been cultivated for generations. Around 20 are opening up every year, according to a recent study.

Known locally as obruks, sinkholes are not a new geological phenomenon. They have existed in the Konya basin for thousands of years, but they have become far more frequent over recent decades.

Konya’s sinkholes are consequently both a geological hazard and evidence of a wider water-management problem. The cavities beneath the fields are the product of geological processes extending over thousands of years. Their recent instability, however, is occurring within a groundwater system profoundly altered by human activity and increasingly exposed to drought.

title: Booker prize 2026: a diverse list to inspire all sorts of readers – six experts review the nominees
content:
When the Booker prize was first launched in 1969, its aim was to get more people reading and to stimulate discussion about contemporary literature. Now, we all know reading is at an all time low but there really has never been a better time to reignite your love of fiction and to discover (or rediscover) your love of reading. And, this year’s shortlist is really a testament to the breadth of stories available out there.

There’s poetic historic fiction with May we Feed the King about a reluctant medieval king from Rebecca Perry. For lovers of science fiction, M. John Harrison has written a tale about aliens and social collapse set on the Kentish coast. And, there’s laughter to be found in Black Bag by Luke Kennard about an out-of-work actor who lands a gig in a psychological experiment.

There are also new works by previous winners and nominees. Marlon James is back with a startling portrait of the lives of gay men in Jamaica. Douglas Stuart gives us his chilly Hebridean family drama, John of John. And, finally there’s the gentle political commentary of Elizabeth Strout’s The Things We Never Say about what happens when good people stay quiet.

title: Dracula saapui halloweeniksi Turun Humalistonkadulle
content:
Liisa Vähäkylä

Turkulainen Linnateatteri toimii Humalistonkadulla entisen elokuvateatteri Dominon tiloissa. Aikanaan Turun suurimman elokuvateatterin katsomossa istutaan pöytien ääressä. Useimmilla pöydillä on viinilaseja ja laseissa punaviiniä, kun Dracula – Karmiva komedia saa ensi-illan.

Tarjolla on kauhua ja rakkautta, elämöintiä ja erotiikkaa sekä parodiaa Bram Stokerin goottiklassikosta. Näytelmäksi nimellä Dracula, A Comedy Of Terrors sen muokkasivat amerikkalaiset käsikirjoittajat Gordon Greenberg ja Steve Rosen viittauksilla Rocky Horror Picture Show -elokuvaan. Koska nimiosan tehnyt Tim Curry kuoli elokuussa, osuu klassinen Dracula-tarina näillä aineksilla ajan hermoon.

Turussakin britti Chris Whittakerin ohjauksessa Draculan sisääntulot muistuttavat kulttielokuvan kohtauksia. Lavasteissa ollaan hillittyjä mutta kekseliäitä. Osa koomisuudesta syntyy pienistä mutta oikein ajoitetuista törmäyksistä.

    The first snow of the approaching winter did not fall in Lapland, but rather in the Kainuu region, in northeastern Finland. In much of the country, a lasting snow cover is likely still a long way off. Nevertheless, the snow season has been declared open in connection with the National Snow Seminar. The declaration marking the start of the snow season (text below) also encourages citizens to observation of snow.

    The 14th National Snow Seminar (Pyryn päivä) was held on October 29–30, 2026, at the Finnish Meteorological Institute’s Arctic Space Centre in Sodankylä. The seminar was organized by the Finnish Meteorological Institute in collaboration with the Finnish Environment Institute (SYKE), as well as the universities of Lapland and Oulu.

title: Mitä uutta Sápmái Buorrin -projektissa?
Serbian opiskelijaliike voitti poliittisten maailmankuvien yhteentörmäyksen
content:
Autoritäärisyyteen valuneessa Serbiassa opiskelijaliikkeen voitto osoitti ruohonjuuritason politiikan voiman. Seuraavaksi olisi ryhdyttävä purkamaan pitkään rakennettua autoritääristä järjestelmää.

Sunnuntai-iltana 25. lokakuuta 2026 Belgradissa oli poikkeuksellinen juhlahumu. Istuva presidentti, autoritäärisistä otteistaan tunnettu Aleksandar Vučić oli juuri ilmoittanut televisiossa, että häntä vastaan vaaleissa asettunut opiskelijoiden lista oli voittanut parlamenttiin enemmistön.

Ennen Vučićin puhetta vaalien lopputulosta ei osannut ennustaa kukaan. Iltapäivällä tihkui tietoja äänestyspaikoille kuljetetuista oudoista äänestäjistä: ilmeisesti monia käytettiin äänestämässä useammassa paikassa. Presidentin tiedettiin etukäteen käyttävän hämäriä keinoja, esimerkiksi äänten ostamista ja Bosnian serbitasavallan äänestäjien hyödyntämistä. Median kontrollista nyt puhumattakaan.

Vaali-ilta eteni nopeasti. Etukäteen monet olivat ennakoineet, että tulos saatettaisiin kiistää tai ainakin jumittaa oikeusjuttuihin yksittäisten äänestyspaikkojen väitetyistä epäselvyyksistä. Vaalihuoneistojen sulkemisesta ei kuitenkaan ollut kulunut kuin puolitoista tuntia, kun Vučić sanoi pelin olevan selvä.

title: SYNTALES – A New International Project Involving Our UNESCO Chair Funded by Creative Europe
content:
We are pleased to announce that SYNTALES (Synthetic Tales About Living Heritage Resilience in Emergencies: Ukrainian Women’s Narratives), an international project involving our UNESCO Chair, has been awarded funding under the European Union’s Creative Europe programme.

The project focuses on safeguarding intangible cultural heritage in contexts of war and forced displacement. It addresses three cultural practices maintained by Ukrainian women: the porridge tradition of Avdiivka, the Karaim hospitality practice of et aiaklat in Melitopol, and Ukrainian Christmas Eve traditions.

Over 24 months, SYNTALES will combine ethnographic fieldwork with generative artificial intelligence. Working alongside Ukrainian artists, participating women will co-create visual representations of their cultural practices, stories, and experiences. The resulting materials will be presented in an exhibition at the National Museum of the History of Ukraine in the Second World War in Kyiv.

Our UNESCO Chair will be responsible for developing the project’s ethical framework, guiding the responsible use of artificial intelligence in documenting and representing living cultural heritage.

title: Huijarit esiintyvät poliiseina ja pankkien edustajina Google Meet -videopuheluissa
content:
Traficomin Kyberturvallisuuskeskukselle on viime viikkoina ilmoitettu aiempaa enemmän huijauksia, joissa rikolliset esiintyvät videopuheluissa poliiseina tai pankkien edustajina.

Huijauspuheluita on soitettu Google Meet -videopuhelupalvelun välityksellä, mikä poikkeaa tavanomaisista puhelimitse tehdyistä huijauspuheluista. Huijauksissa on käytetty tunnettujen poliisien kasvoja, ja tapauksissa epäillään hyödynnetyn tekoälyllä tuotettua väärennettyä videokuvaa.

Rikolliset pyrkivät hankkimaan uhrien pankkitunnuksia, maksukorttitietoja ja muita henkilötietoja. Uhria voidaan painostaa uhkaamalla esimerkiksi tilien sulkemisella, pidätyksellä tai maasta karkottamisella. Pankkien nimissä tehdyissä huijauksissa voidaan väittää, että tilillä on epäilyttävää toimintaa tai että varojen turvaaminen edellyttää välittömiä toimenpiteitä. Kiireen ja pelon avulla uhri yritetään saada luovuttamaan tietonsa tai siirtämään rahaa rikollisille.

title: Etla 80-juhlaseminaari näytti suuntaa tulevaisuuteen
content:
Etla täytti tänä syksynä 80 vuotta, mutta emme tyytyneet vain juhlimaan itseämme vaan käytimme juhlavuoden näyttämään suuntaa Suomen tulevaisuuteen. Julkaisimme juhlakirjan ”Suomi 2051”, jossa toimme julkisuuteen konkreettisen toimenpidelistan ja julistimme sodan apatiaa vastaan. Etla 80-juhlaseminaari syyskuussa näytti suuntaa tulevaisuuteen ja saimme keskusteluun mukaan myös tasavallan presidentin. Koostevideolta voit palata vielä seminaarin tunnelmiin.

Vuonna 1946 perustettu Elinkeinoelämän tutkimuslaitos ETLA täytti 80 vuotta kuluvana vuonna. Pitkä ikä on asiantuntijaorganisaatiolle voimavara ja uskottavuuttakin vahvistava tekijä, mutta siihen liittyy samalla vaara leimautua menneisyyden pölyiseksi instituutioksi.

Olimme havainneet jo ennen juhlavuotta, että Suomen talous on polkenut paikallaan kaksi vuosikymmentä ja samaan aikaan julkinen keskustelu on ollut näköalatonta ja lyhytjänteistä, apaattistakin. Päätimme ottaa 80-vuotisjuhlavuoden strategiseksi tavoitteeksi kääntää koko juhlavuosi Suomen  haasteisiin vastaamiseksi.

title: Russia: The Revolt of the Letter-Writers
content:
In the days around October 30, Russia’s Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Political Repression, at least 160 gatherings have been planned to commemorate and support prisoners of conscience.  

Most will bring people together, often after public readings of the names of victims of Soviet repression, to write to today’s political prisoners, of whom around 1,800 have been formally recognized, though the true number is closer to 5,000. The evenings will span Russia from Kaliningrad to Vladivostok, with events abroad in places as diverse as Seattle and Seoul.  

Organizers represent a broad range of communities, including supporters of murdered opposition leader Alexei Navalny, regional branches of the liberal Yabloko party, a feminist anarchist collective and a grassroots educational initiative which writes to jailed students and scientists. 

Solidarity with political prisoners has become a powerful shared cause for Russians in exile and those who remain in the country, drawing people into collective action, as documented in a CEPA report in June.

title: Mark Carney puts deadline on EU ‘associate membership’ push
content:
MONTREAL — Canada embraced the European Union’s offer of “associate membership” after a two-day summit at which Brussels and Ottawa gave themselves until next June to work out what their new relationship will look like.

Prime Minister Mark Carney’s endorsement of the proposal by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen followed weeks of hesitation, a hostile response from U.S. President Donald Trump and pushback from EU heavyweight Germany.

“In the coming months, we will determine the full substance, scale, and scope of this new form of membership,” Carney told a press conference on Friday at the end of the two-day summit at the Port of Montreal. 

“Today, we move towards associate membership for Canada,” Carney said, describing it as “the deepest possible partnership short of accession.”

The two sides have set a June 2027 deadline to determine the terms and boundaries of their intensifying relationship — an alliance that comes with a payment schedule. Carney danced around a question pressing him on how much associate membership will cost the Canadian public.

“We don’t view this as paying, personally,” Carney said, stressing the alliance as a “positive” project.

title: The letters that gave five human rights activists hope
content:
For the past 25 years, Amnesty International’s Write for Rights campaign has been bringing people together to fight for justice and dignity. Millions of people have changed the lives of those whose human rights had been stripped from them, giving them hope in times of darkness.

Amnesty’s brilliant supporters have written letters both to those whose rights are being violated, and the people in authority who can make change happen.

For many, a simple letter made so much difference, letting them know that there were people out there rooting for them.

Here, five people who were part of Amnesty’s Write for Rights campaign share a letter that meant the most to them…

Wendy Galarza was shot after attending a protest in Cancún, Mexico. She almost lost her life speaking out for women’s rights in her country. She lodged a complaint against the police, though it took months for the State Prosecutor to accept her additional evidence, which included clothing showing bullet holes from the day of the protest. While the case continues, Wendy has set up a collective with other persons who were assaulted that day.

title: How the streets and a social media army led Lula to a historic win in Brazil
content:
For the first time in the country, a candidate managed to turn the results in the run-off

Originally published on Global Voices

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva waves Brazil’s flag surrounded by a crowd of supporters in São Paulo, during the 2026 election campaign. Photo by Ricardo Stuckert/Lula Oficial on Flickr (CC BY-SA 4.0).

On April 7, 2018, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who had been president of Brazil twice, waited in the building of the Metalworkers’ Union, in São Bernardo do Campo, São Paulo state, where his political life started in the 1970s, to be arrested by the Federal Police following convictions for corruption and money laundering.

Gilberto Carvalho, one of his oldest allies, later recalled that they hoped for a crowd of 50,000, but only 10,000 people waited outside. Lula looked through the window, grabbed his arm, and said, “Gilbertinho, we go to war with the soldiers we have.”

Eight years and six months after that day, on October 25, 2026, Lula was elected president of Brazil for the fourth time, supported by millions of people in the streets and an army of his own online.

title: OPINION: Country Before Party: Israel’s Opposition Must Not Fail This Moment
content:
The election has opened a path away from Netanyahu’s disastrous rule. Israel’s opposition must now choose: build a Jewish-Arab governing partnership or risk surrendering the country’s future to the forces tearing it apart.

By Alon Ben-Meir*|

NEW YORK | 30 October 2026 (IDN) — Israel stands at a historic crossroads. The government that emerges from this election will determine whether the country begins to repair its democracy and recover its moral bearings—or continues toward deeper division, international isolation, and the erosion of its founding promise.

For Israel’s opposition, this is no ordinary coalition negotiation. It tests whether its leaders have the courage to put country before party, personal ambition, and ideological prejudice.

The parliamentary arithmetic offers an opening. The completed count gives parties opposed to Benjamin Netanyahu a combined 67 of the Knesset’s 120 seats: 48 for the Jewish opposition parties and 19 for the Arab-led parties. Netanyahu’s bloc holds 53. These numbers create an opportunity to replace him, not an agreement on how to govern.

title: Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups denounce UAE nominee for UN top job
content:
Critics cite Lana Nusseibeh’s denial of accusations the UAE is fuelling Sudan war by supporting paramilitary RSF

Members of the Sudanese diaspora and international human rights monitors have denounced the candidature of an Emirati diplomat for the top job at the UN, citing her denial of accusations that the United Arab Emirates is fuelling the war in Sudan by supporting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

The UAE nominated Lana Nusseibeh last week to replace the UN secretary general, António Guterres, as he finishes his second five-year term ⁠this year, upending a race that had become gridlocked.

title: Europe is a pumpkin paradise
content: Europe has developed quite an appetite for pumpkins, a crop that isn't native to the continent. More than 1.2 million tonnes were harvested in Europe last year. So how did pumpkins become a Halloween staple? The answer lies in the origins of Halloween, a tradition millions of Scottish and Irish immigrants brought to the United States in the 1800s. They celebrated Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival marking the end of summer and harvest season. To ward off spirits, people hollowed out hard root vegetables like turnips and carved frightening faces into the rind before placing a candle inside. In America, where turnips were scarce, pumpkins offered a convenient alternative. Much easier to carve, they became the defining symbol of Halloween. The tradition has since travelled back across the Atlantic, bringing the pumpkin along with it. Perhaps Europe is taking back Halloween, one pumpkin at a time. Writer’s note: I carved my first pumpkin last weekend, and if that was a struggle, I have no idea how anyone managed to carve a raw turnip without losing a finger.

title: Scientists Analyzed Thousands of Psychedelic Trips. They Found Something Disturbing
content:
Researchers have amassed a trove of more than 25,000 calls to a support hotline for people during and after psychedelic trips, making it “the largest dataset of psychedelic support interactions ever assembled—exceeding the combined sample sizes of all published psychedelic clinical trials by an order of magnitude,” according to a study published on Friday in Science Advances.

Despite the popularity of psychedelics as recreational drugs, and increasing interest in them as medically-prescribed therapeutic treatments, there is very little research about the effects of these substances outside of clinical settings with carefully-selected patients. That, scientists say, is limiting what we can learn about the effects of these drugs, because the vast majority of psychedelics are consumed by all kinds of people in homes, festivals, ceremonial gatherings, or other uncontrolled environments.    

The Fireside Project, a nonprofit founded in 2020, has filled this knowledge gap with its Psychedelic Support Line, which connects callers who are on bad trips, or who are seeking more information about psychedelics, with trained volunteers who offer confidential peer support.

title: Defanging Laws and Bringing Home Billions: How Trump Has Rewritten the Corruption Rulebook At Home and Abroad
content:
During his first term in office, U.S. President Donald J. Trump drew criticism for profiting from events held at Trump-branded golf courses and housing foreign delegations at his pricey Washington hotel. 

But upon his return, he has blown past all precedents on personal enrichment while also overseeing the systematic unraveling of American anti-corruption laws, institutions, and norms. 

While many of these moves have been enforced by the U.S. government’s executive branch, the Republican-led Congress has done little to stop the slide — and, in some cases, has even encouraged it.

So when U.S. voters head to the polls on November 3 for midterm elections, it is not just control of the House of Representatives and the Senate that is at stake, but the future of efforts to contain corruption at home and abroad. 

On the eve of the election, OCCRP spoke to experts to take stock of the state of U.S. corruption — and the fight against it —  today, whether Democrats have a plan to reverse course, and what the repercussions of Trump’s actions have been at home and abroad. 

The White House did not respond to requests to comment in time for publication.

title: How a Secret Vote by U.N. Scientists Legitimized Carbon Capture and Skewed Decades of Climate Policy
content:
From the series Carbon Captured: How the fossil fuel industry influence climate research, an investigation from ProPublica and Drilled

In the spring of 2005, the United Nations convened more than 100 of the world’s top scientists in the medieval town of Oviedo, Spain. They were there to finish writing a paradigm-shifting report about a technology that they hoped could help stop climate change. 

To celebrate the report’s impending completion, the meeting’s hosts handed out bottles of cava, Spanish sparkling wine, with tongue-in-cheek labels stating that they were to be opened only by those who truly believed it could work.

Belief was necessary because the technology — carbon capture and storage, or CCS — had barely been tested. The idea was simple: strip carbon dioxide from smokestacks before it could flow into the air and warm the planet. Then pump it into a porous part of the Earth’s crust and leave it there. Forever.

title: How the Sphinx is helping answer a riddle about extinct crocodiles
content:
My colleagues and I discovered a new species of extinct crocodile from a fossil found in the same rocks used to carve the Great Sphinx of Giza.

Today, there are only two species of the long-snouted gavial crocodile, both of which are endangered: Gavialis gangeticus and Tomistoma schlegelii. They are found only in freshwater environments on the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

However, the fossil record of gavials goes back 80 million years, to the time of the dinosaurs. It shows that they were once diverse, with more than 40 species known, and lived all over the globe. So how did a group of crocodiles that today cannot tolerate saltwater once live all over the world? Our discovery may help to solve this puzzle.

Although the distribution of the continents differed from today, most were already separated by oceans. My colleagues and I have been trying to understand how gavials achieved this cosmopolitan distribution, while also seeking to unlock what led to their current predicament.

title: ‘What we leave behind is not as important as how we’ve lived’: remembering actor Patrick Stewart
content:
At the end of Star Trek: Generations (1994), surveying the wreckage of the crashed USS Enterprise he captained for nearly a decade, Jean-Luc Picard (Patrick Stewart) muses to his first officer, William Riker (Jonathan Frakes):

… time is a companion that goes with us on the journey, reminds us to cherish every moment, because it will never come again. What we leave behind is not as important as how we’ve lived.

… time is a companion that goes with us on the journey, reminds us to cherish every moment, because it will never come again. What we leave behind is not as important as how we’ve lived.

Smiling, he quips to Riker, “After all, Number One, we’re only mortal.”

Passing away this week at 86 years old, we are sadly reminded of that mortality with the death of Sir Patrick Stewart: actor, dramaturge, Shakespearean exemplar, mutant professor, and distinguished Starfleet captain.

Born in Mirfield, England, in 1940, Stewart grew up poor during the worst days of the second world war.

He found his calling to theatre as a child, thanks to a keen-eyed English teacher and a copy of Shakespeare’s plays.

He left school at 15 to become a working actor in community theatre.

title: Uusi tutkimus korostaa hyönteisten monipuolista merkitystä selkärankaisille
content:
Mitä yhteistä on simpansseilla, papukaijoilla, harmaakarhuilla, lepakoilla ja laiskiaisilla? Uusi tutkimus osoittaa, että nämä ja monet muut selkärankaiset ovat eri tavoin riippuvaisia hyönteisistä, ja hyönteisten biodiversiteetillä on selkärankaisille huomattava merkitys.

Lähes kolme neljännestä niistä maalla ja makeissa vesissä elävistä selkärankaisista, joiden ruokavaliosta on tietoa, syö selkärangattomia, ja yli kaksi viidesosaa syö pelkästään niitä. Hyönteiset muodostavat ruokavaliosta usein suurimman osan. Tulos käy ilmi Nature Reviews Biodiversity -lehdessä tänä syksynä julkaistusta katsausartikkelista.

Ruoka on kuitenkin vain yksi osa vaikutussuhteita. Haikarat käyttävät hyönteisiä syöttinä houkutellakseen kaloja. Tietyt myrkylliset sammakot saavat myrkkynsä syömällä muurahaisia ja kovakuoriaisia. Yöperhoset edistävät laiskiaisten turkissa kasvavan levän kasvua, ja levä on laiskiaisille tärkeä ravinnonlähde.

Hyönteiset vaikuttavat selkärankaisiin myönteisesti, kielteisesti ja välillisesti. Ne tarjoavat ravintoa, rakenteita, puhtautta ja suojaa, mutta voivat myös aiheuttaa tauteja tai toimia jopa saalistajina.

title: Potilasasiavastaavaan voi ottaa yhteyttä OmaSavossa 2. marraskuuta alkaen
content:
Hyvinvointialueen digitaaliseen OmaSavo-palveluun avataan 2. marraskuuta alkaen uusi viestit-palvelu potilasasiavastaaville. Asiakkaat voivat ottaa viestit-palvelun kautta yhteyttä potilasasiavastaavaan silloin, kun heidän asiallaan ei ole kiire.

Potilasasiavastaavat neuvovat ja tukevat asiakkaita potilaan asemaan ja oikeuksiin liittyvissä asioissa sekä auttavat selvittämään hoitoon ja palveluun liittyviä epäselvyyksiä.

- Asiakas voi ottaa yhteyttä potilasasiavastaavaan, jos hän tarvitsee neuvoja potilaan oikeuksiin liittyvissä asioissa tai haluaa keskustella saamastaan hoidosta tai kohtelusta, HYTE- ja osallisuuspäällikkö Säde Rytkönen kertoo.

Potilasasiavastaavan tehtävä on neuvoa ja ohjata. Hän ei ota kantaa hoitopäätöksiin, hoidon toteutumiseen tai siihen, onko hoidossa tapahtunut potilasvahinko. Potilasasiavastaava ei myöskään tulkitse potilasasiakirjojen sisältöä.

Vuonna 2025 asiakkaat ottivat yhteyttä potilasasiavastaaviin 3 170 kertaa. Näistä 1 594 yhteydenottoa koski KYSiä tai muuta erikoissairaanhoitoa ja 1 576 terveyskeskusten toimintaa.

title: Germany’s Security Consensus Assailed by Left and Right
content:
Recent months have brought electoral success in Germany for three parties on the populist extremes that challenge the country’s current security and foreign policy, albeit for different reasons: AfD, BSW and Die Linke. Might they pose a challenge to eight decades of broad European security consensus? 

The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), whose electoral support surged to record highs in the recent elections in the east German states of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Saxony-Anhalt, is pushing for a softer line on Moscow: its Bundestag caucus has called for German weapons deliveries to Ukraine to stop, and for sanctions on Russia to be rolled back as part of peace talks. AfD politicians have also been involved in controversies related to their travel to Russia.

title: Why VPNs Are Worth Defending
content:
Developers of virtual private network (VPN) apps are reporting that their products are again being pulled from Apple’s App Store in Russia. This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Why? VPNs give people a way to control their own online activities. When you visit a website through a VPN, that website only sees the VPN server's location (well, IP address) rather than your actual location. It's like sending a letter through a P.O. box so the recipient doesn't know where you really live. It can also disguise where you’re accessing information from, which can make it possible to access information banned by your government.

This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

title: EU open to flexibility on euro and Schengen if UK tries to rejoin
content:
LONDON — Brussels would be flexible on letting Britain stay out of the euro and the Schengen area if it applied to rejoin the European Union, two EU officials familiar with the bloc’s approach have told POLITICO.

Britain would not necessarily have to join the single currency or passport-free zone — a concern held by some British voters — according to the two officials, who were granted anonymity to speak freely about a sensitive matter.

Opening the door for the U.K. to return to the bloc on similar terms would be a serious boost to the prospects of restoring the country’s EU membership, and a rejection of those who have argued it shouldn’t be allowed back in without joining the euro or Schengen.

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Brexit isn’t working — and even suggested rejoining the EU could make it into Labour’s next election manifesto.

But some euroskeptics say a returning Britain would likely be strong-armed into making commitments to European integration that go beyond the membership deal it had before Brexit.

title: How one Haitian entrepreneur found success by supporting all things local
content:
‘Let us eat what we produce; that way, we all win’

Originally published on Global Voices

REB Lokal founder Rébetha Charles stands with a jar of peanut butter (manba lokal). Photo courtesy of Rébetha Charles, used with permission.

For several decades, due to the significant reduction of tariff barriers on foreign goods — particularly those from the United States and the Dominican Republic — Haiti has depended heavily on imported products for local consumption.

The arrangement began under various structural adjustment programmes that were initiated between 1994 and 1995, through agreements between the Haitian government and international financial institutions like the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. Since then, imports have practically invaded the Haitian market, creating inequitable competition for local farmers who rely on subsistence agriculture and traditional, rudimentary equipment, and significantly weakening national production.

title: “They Killed Us”
content:
When I woke up this morning to the news that Novaya Gazeta is closing its doors, it felt like a personal blow. To me, Novaya’s office in a small grey building in central Moscow always felt like home. 

The newsroom moved to Moscow almost three decades ago. I got to know its every nook and cranny, as I went there, in my capacity of a Moscow-based Human Rights Watch researcher, for meetings, celebrations, commemorations, or simply to swap stories with a friendly journalist over coffee or wine.

I was there on the night of Anna Politkovskaya’s murder in October 2006 and stood outside seven years later as her memorial plaque was affixed to the wall. I celebrated with the newsroom when editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021. For years, I worked alongside Novaya journalists in conflict zones. Together, we travelled to Chechnya, remote mountain villages in Dagestan, South Ossetia (Georgia), and Ukraine. It was more than collaboration; it was a true partnership.

title: Proton’s CEO Cancels AI ‘Re-Interviews’
content:
On Friday, Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, cancelled a series of nearly company-wide ‘re-interviews’ that would have forced employees to explain how they are using AI, with the clear intention that they may be fired if not using it enough in the eyes of Proton leadership, according to six current Proton employees and audio of an around two hour all-hands meeting obtained by 404 Media.

The move came after 404 Media published an investigation on Thursday, which showed how Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton, in some cases despite security concerns from employees. In one exchange, an employee in the company’s security Slack channel urged Proton to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure,” Yen wrote in the channel at the end of August. “Stop thinking always of how to be slower, and focus more on how to be faster.” Yen added, “stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more.”

title: Five Questions About Trump’s ‘America First’ Approach to Fighting Corruption
content:
Shortly after taking office in early 2025, the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump paused the enforcement of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), the nearly 50-year-old law that prohibits American citizens or companies from bribing foreign officials for business.

When the FCPA was resumed six months later, the U.S. Department of Justice was ordered to narrow its focus to limit “undue burdens” on American companies operating outside the country. That action was in line with the Trump administration’s “America First” unilateral approach to foreign policy, which has seen the U.S. withdraw from dozens of international organizations on the grounds that they are inefficient and not in line with the country’s priorities. 

Lorenzo Crippa, a lecturer at the University of Strathclyde who quantitatively studies how recorded instances of corruption affect financial flows, discusses the repercussions of these changes and worrying trends that have emerged under the new U.S. approach to global anti-corruption enforcement.

title: Federal and State Officials Ramp Up Scrutiny of DraftKings, Other Sports Betting Apps
content:
State and federal officials have ramped up scrutiny of online sports betting companies in recent weeks, launching inquiries, demanding information and, in one case, proposing a new rule that would limit when companies like DraftKings can pitch their users to bet more.

The moves — by gaming regulators, government lawyers and federal lawmakers — follow an investigation last month by ProPublica that tested the guardrails DraftKings and other sports betting companies have in place to protect users from spiraling out of control. That system is called responsible gaming, and executives say it’s integral to their companies’ long-term success.

The ProPublica article showed how DraftKings bestowed VIP status on a reporter who deliberately bet like a problem gambler. The report detailed the ways in which the app’s user design and promotions encouraged more betting — even after the reporter opted into responsible gaming tools designed to slow users down. A week earlier, The New York Times reported that DraftKings had used machine learning and artificial intelligence to target promotions to losing bettors.

title: How Ireland plans to beat the data center backlash
content:
TALLAGHT, Ireland — In a suburban industrial park south of Dublin, a sprawling mass of tubes, vents and steel stretches as far as the eye can see, forming a dense web of gray monoliths that encircle the city.

As the EU’s tech capital, where most of the world’s technology giants have their European headquarters, Ireland was ground zero for the backlash against the energy-guzzling data centers needed to power the promised revolution of artificial intelligence.

Dublin is now leading an experiment within Europe to force tech firms to invest in renewable energy. As pushback spreads across Europe and data centers prove a hot-button issue for the U.S. midterm elections, that puts Ireland at the vanguard of countries globally that are trying to quell voter anger over financial and environmental disruptions caused by data centers.

Back in 2021, Ireland was far ahead of the curve in slamming the brakes on data centers as its utilities regulator almost entirely halted new facilities connecting to the creaking electricity grid around Dublin. Authorities warned that the exploding data center industry posed a “significant” risk to the security of the country’s electricity supply.

title: Critic of Mali’s Junta Forcibly Disappeared Six Months On
content:
Six months after their abductions, Mountaga Tall, an outspoken critic of Mali’s junta, and his son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, remain missing, their fate unknown, and the Malian authorities silent. Every day that passes without news raises fears for their safety and deepens their family’s anguish.

Unidentified gunmen abducted Tall in Bamako, Mali’s capital, on May 2. Tall’s son went missing on May 16 after receiving a call informing him that he could deliver belongings to his father, who was reportedly being held at an undisclosed location.

Radio France Internationale reported in July that the United Nations Committee on Enforced Disappearances had urged Mali’s authorities to locate and protect Tall and his son.

International media suggest that Malian intelligence services may be holding Tall in a secret facility. Malian authorities, however, have neither acknowledged detaining Tall or his son nor provided information about their location, legal status, or health, despite requests from Tall’s family and a legal team.

title: Behind the Blog: Tech Support
content:
This is Behind the Blog, where we share our behind-the-scenes thoughts about how a few of our top stories of the week came together. This week, we discuss customer service and Proton fallout.

JASON: Since I wrote about ChatGPT turning me into tech support for people’s random problems, I have gotten many more AI-generated emails from people asking me to solve their tech support problems. So, mission accomplished I guess. I think and hope it was clear in the article, but I think this phenomenon is happening to a lot of journalists, not just us at 404 Media. A lot of the ChatGPT chats I saw told people to reach out to multiple journalists, and gave them contact info and instructions on how to do so. Some suggested that they reach out to lawyers or academic researchers as well, so I assume it’s all sorts of people who are getting this new type of spam.
